en/solve/solv-buy-phone-plan.title: How to pick the right cell phone plan for you?
en/solve/solv-buy-phone-plan.summary: A mobile plan that actually fits what you need and what you can afford.
en/solve/solv-buy-phone-plan.content:
Hi, I’m Nicolás, and just like you, I’ve been learning step-by-step how to improve my connectivity.
I’m no expert, but through searching the Internet, watching tutorials, and above all, trial and error, I’ve learned a ton and set up some functional solutions.
What does buying the right cell phone plan mean?
Below, you’ll find a series of information, criteria, and tips that aim to be as clear as possible, so you can feel supported when making the decision about which Smartphone plan to buy.
The estimated reading time is about 9 minutes and it consists of 10 items, but don’t panic, you can read these items with the help of others. Remember that at SOLE Voltaje, we want to promote the collective use of the internet.

What is this for?
In this solution, you’ll find some practical tips to help you make a much more informed decision about which cell phone plans are best for you.

Before we start, some ethical considerations
At SOLE Voltaje, we like to clarify the ethical implications of the decisions we make, and we like to focus on the circumstances that lead you to make that decision. We often use uncomfortable questions to challenge ourselves.
Shall we play? You want to buy a cell phone plan with data, but do you really need it? Think about it; it might not be the best option for you.
Sometimes, you have free internet at public libraries. Maybe you can use a neighbor’s WiFi signal, or you can buy a cell phone PIN to access the Internet for a few hours.
If, after scanning your options, you definitely decide you need to buy a cell phone plan, this is the right place for you! Here, we’ll advise you on which prepaid and postpaid internet plans might be useful.

What do you need?

Money saved for the purchase
Information on available operators
A place where you can top up or subscribe to the plan
Curiosity


How to do it?

ALERT! Before you start: prepaid or postpaid?
To have clarity when reading this solution, we first need to address some concepts. In this case, the difference between a postpaid and a prepaid plan.

























PrepaidPostpaidYou pay for mobile services before using them.You pay for mobile services after using them.You can top up whenever you want.You’ll have to pay your bill month by month.You can get your prepaid plan by subscription or on-demand.It helps build your credit history.You don’t get a monthly bill.It gives you additional benefits like cheaper rates.
There is no absolute answer as to which type of service to choose. It depends on each person’s habits, possibilities, and needs.

Step 0 → Decide if you need a cell phone plan

One of the characteristics of our current era is the great development of international and national markets. Our cell phones are made in China and we can buy them in Colombia; we can go to the market and buy rice brought from Brazil. Furthermore, we find disproportionate consumption options: we can buy white rice, yellow rice, bulk rice, lemon-flavored rice, etc.
There are endless options to turn us into consumers of products that, many times, we don’t need. Thus, we end up buying non-nutritious food and falling into expenses that don’t satisfy the main function of eating.
Similarly, we fill our homes with endless merchandise that ends up gathering dust or being thrown away because, in the end, it was useless to us.
At SOLE Colombia, we want to promote responsible consumption.
Is choosing your cell phone data plan a responsible choice? We encourage you to answer the following questions:

Do you need to buy a cell phone plan, or do you have other options to access the internet?
Is there any other option that could cover your internet connection and be paid for by several people?
If you buy a cell phone plan, will it really improve your quality of life, or will it make it worse? How much time will you spend on social media? Will it be hard for you to disconnect from the content? Will it imply a monthly dose of stress knowing how you’ll pay for this new expense?
Finally, is this new consumption really a priority for you? What real use will you give it?
Don’t forget this consideration: the decision you make can be reversible when conditions change. It’s not a child; it’s just a payment plan that you can change whenever and however you need to.




Step 1 → Identify what you need the plan for

Now that you’ve decided, it’s time to understand what you’re going to need it for.
Do you need the plan to facilitate your work, to study, to stay connected with family and friends, or to spend leisure time? Depending on your answer, you’ll identify usage patterns.
Let’s use my case as an example:

💡 In 2022, I had two jobs and no office. Plus, I moved around a lot: I traveled around Bogotá and to different parts of the country frequently. I needed to connect to virtual meetings; one of my jobs required Zoom video calls. So, I needed a data connection and to make calls to many people. At that time, I decided to get a postpaid plan with 10 GB and unlimited minutes.
Shortly after, I started traveling and staying constantly at a family farm, where the data signal was very bad. I decided to buy a fixed internet plan for the farm.
In 2023, I only had one job and had an office with internet. I didn’t need to travel as much anymore. I changed my postpaid plan to a cheaper one and canceled the internet plan at the farm.

Now it’s your turn to identify what you need the internet plan for!


Step 2 → Ask yourself the right questions based on your needs


Do you need minutes, data, or both?
Do you need a high connection speed to download heavy files or have video calls?
Do you need to have this service constantly, or is it only for a few days of the week?
Do you need coverage in several territories or just one?
What budget do you have available for this expense?




Step 3 → Investigate what is available

Now let’s take action! We need to get the following information:
Which mobile operators are available in my area?

Ask your neighbors: what operator do they use or have they used in the past? Which one works best? Which one has better technical support? Which one has better rates?
You can go to cell phone stores in the nearest urban center and ask directly about which operators they have available. In Colombia for 2024, there are multiple options: Claro, Movistar, TIGO, WOM, Virgin Mobile, Avantel, and Móvil Éxito are the main operators in the market. The latter two are small operators that rent the infrastructure of the big operators to provide their services.

What plans do these operators have available?
After being clear about the operators available in your territory and knowing which ones perform best, proceed to ask about the prepaid and postpaid plans they offer. Below, we present some comparative tables of the prepaid and postpaid plans offered in 2023.
Prepaid plan rates 7-10 days

Selectra, What is the best prepaid cell phone plan in Colombia?


Step 4 → Evaluate the best option for you

It’s time to make a decision! With the information you gathered, we’ll give you some criteria that we consider fundamental when making a decision:

Frequency of use, how much will you use it?


Photo: Pixabay License
If, for example, most of your days you need to make calls and be connected to the internet, balancing it out, postpaid plans end up being the best option.
But if, on the other hand, your demand is occasional, has variability throughout the month, and/or you can be constantly connected to a WiFi network at your workplace or home, making sporadic prepaid top-ups might be the most useful.

Budget, how much money do you want to spend?

Now it’s time to define a budget! An easy calculation: how many hours of work per week does this new expense represent? This can become a permanent expense, so it’s important to reason through the purchase.
The final decision might fall on this point: people who use prepaid plans usually don’t have a constant flow of money that guarantees they can pay a monthly fee. While the use of postpaid is associated with people who can guarantee the payment of a monthly fee constantly.
Currently, prepaid top-ups in the Colombian market start from 2,000 COP with one day of validity.** On the other hand, the cheapest postpaid plans are around **27,000 COP per month.
To make this decision, take stock of how much you are willing to invest in this service and what your frequency of use is.

Usage habits, what and how will you use it for?

Are you a person who makes long-duration calls, or do you spend more time connected to the internet? Depending on this, you can prioritize the number of minutes, the number of Gigabytes, or both, when choosing your consumption option.
Below, we explain each of these variables if you are still not very clear about how they work:













MinutesDataThe minutes associated with your plan determine how long you can spend talking to other mobile phones nationwide; in some cases, a number of minutes to other countries like Venezuela, Canada, or the United States is also included. Currently, most postpaid plans come with unlimited minutes.These are the amount of mobile data intended for internet use on your phone. Their use is the amount your cell phone uploads or downloads when using them. You can configure them to not spend them, save them, or restrict what they are used for. Remember that depending on the content you upload or download, data consumption will be higher or lower; for example, watching a two-hour movie from your cell phone can consume approximately 300 MB, almost a third of a Gigabyte. Content like high-resolution videos, audio, or images has high data consumption compared to other types of files like text.

Photo: CC0 Public Domain,
For example, when we do a SOLE, we need to connect a few computers to be able to research Big Questions. That means the plan we contract must necessarily have data.
You can make your phone’s Internet connection available to the group so everyone can use it.
Although the internet searches that take place in a SOLE don’t use much data, you might want to watch videos or other content that requires more data than you have contracted. However, you don’t need that amount of data available all the time.
So, you can buy a prepaid plan that allows you to be connected, specifically for the SOLE, and solve your Big Questions.
If you decide to meet once a week or want to have the space available with the connection at any time, you can consider paying for a postpaid plan together… how does that sound?

Signal, where are you going to use it?

We have to look at coverage, upload and download speed, 3G, 4G signal.
Although we often hear people say that one operator is better than another, this will depend on the region and can change over time.
Sometimes they install more antennas or their networks get saturated due to an excess of users.

Other benefits, information that may be useful


Watch out for “Free data usage in apps”
Remember, nothing is free!

Most plans currently in Colombia have the use of applications like Facebook or WhatsApp as “unlimited” as long as the top-up lasts or for the whole month in the case of postpaid plans.
They never explain to us that this unlimited consumption is only related to messages that contain text; that is, if you see a photo or a video on WhatsApp or Facebook, the data associated with this consumption will be deducted from your plan.

‘Free’ applications

Some postpaid plans offer us a license for applications like Amazon Prime (a series and movie platform) or Spotify (a music playback application); that is, for the payment of a cell phone plan, they give you access to the Premium version of these platforms. This can be beneficial if they are platforms you already use; if not, ignore it, it will be one more consumption.
They also don’t tell you that this way of ‘forcing’ you to use certain applications to communicate, entertain yourself, inform yourself, or create your digital presence is part of a commercial strategy. That is, companies will use the information from your profiles to offer you consumer goods, which will redound to the benefit of the corporations responsible for their processing… that is, those companies are profiting from the information they get about you. So, watch out, when a product is free, it’s because you are the product.

Don’t be fooled
It is important that you constantly check the plans and offers of the operators.
Currently, in Colombia, you can do “portability,” that is, switch from one operator to another, change from one operator’s plan to another while keeping your number, just by requesting the new operator to carry out this process. There are no longer permanence clauses that force you to stay with the same operator for a certain time. So if you see that there is a better option for you, don’t hesitate to do portability!
There is a small offer available from small operators; these are prepaid plans with long validity periods.
I, who live in Bogotá, am evaluating switching to Móvil Éxito. I currently have a postpaid plan at WOM where I pay 40,000 COP**, which gives me the right to **60 GB and unlimited minutes**—that's a lot! Initially, I switched to WOM because, by doing portability, they gave me the **first three months free, plus 20GB**, and they **charged me 35,000 COP. Now that I’m in Bogotá and work from home and the office, I have internet available from these places. I was checking options while writing this solution and saw that Móvil Éxito offers the following prepaid plans:

Per month, my consumption does not exceed 5 GB and I make, at most, 30 calls a month. For this reason, the first plan would cost me $13,000 COP, less than a third of what I pay now! Mind you, I have to make the payment for the whole year at once, but I am not tied to any type of contract.

How much is enough?
This question is difficult to answer, but I think we can rephrase it as follows: does the option you chose meet the need and intention you projected at the beginning?
In the previous example, I showed you how I consider the plan I currently have to be excessive and I found options that do meet my initial requirement, at a third of the price I currently pay.
These types of reasoning are what we would like you to have when making a decision about the option you are going to buy.

en/solve/solv-buy-satellite-antenna.title: How to get a satellite dish up and running?
en/solve/solv-buy-satellite-antenna.summary: Pick an internet service for those places where signal is non-existent.
en/solve/solv-buy-satellite-antenna.content:
Photo: Satellite antenna - Wikipedia
Hi, I’m Nicolás and I’m learning how the internet works. I’m no expert, but through online searches, tutorials, and, above all, a lot of curiosity, I’ve learned how to set up functional internet solutions.
What does it mean to choose an internet service for unconnected places?
In this particular solution, we’ll learn how to choose a satellite internet service for rural or remote areas that don’t have Wi-Fi or wired internet connections. To do this, we’ll look at three technologies available in Colombia: Satellite dish, WiMax, and Starlink.

What is it for?
This solution is for getting a clearer picture of which satellite internet service you can choose if you’re located in areas without Wi-Fi or wired internet connections.

How do I know if I need it?
Now, the quality of the internet service you can choose will depend on your possibilities and needs, as well as the availability of internet providers in your region.
This solution is an option you can pay for together with the people in the community where you live. Consult with others to have a common criterion and decide jointly; sharing the decision, care, expenses, benefits, and advantages of the services will make the decision you take more sustainable and long-lasting in the long run.

What do you need?

A budget, meaning knowing what you can spend
A list of internet providers in your region
Lots of curiosity!
It can help to have reference people in your community with whom to review the information; making a decision together will be easier and more beneficial for everyone


How to do it?

Step 0 → What types of internet connections work in unconnected regions?

Now let’s get down to business. Digital technologies change rapidly over the years. In this article, we want to present you with research on the options available in Colombia for 2024: satellite dish, WiMax, and Starlink.

Satellite dish


The most popular internet option for rural or remote areas these days is the satellite dish. The great advantage of this solution is its coverage, accessibility, and price, which makes it a viable and functional option. To access this technology, the company in charge will need to install a satellite dish at your house.

WiMax


Image: Alvarion WiMAX CPE Equipment - Wikipedia
The first thing you need is to contact a company that offers these services and has a repeater near your house to be able to send you the internet signal. Afterward, you have to put an antenna on the facade of your house. This antenna will have to point directly at the company’s repeater that is going to provide the service, or at an intermediate connection point used to bypass obstacles between your antenna and their repeater. The installation of the antenna will be done by the company itself.

Starlink


Image: Starlink Standard Actuated Antenna - Starlink
Starlink is Elon Musk’s satellite internet project. It’s a private satellite internet that facilitates connections, especially in rural areas. The company is considered the world’s first and largest satellite constellation using a low Earth orbit to offer high-speed, low-latency broadband satellite internet, which allows for streaming content, online gaming, video calls, and more.
To get it up and running, you must buy a kit with an antenna that must be placed outside your house, which automatically orients itself to establish a connection in a matter of minutes, provided you have a clear view of the sky.
We already have an introduction to the available options, now we can move on to moment 1 where we will talk about the advantages and disadvantages of each option.


Step 1 → Advantages and disadvantages of the satellite dish connection

Advantages

Global coverage: This means that people living in remote regions or rural areas can access the Internet reliably.
Fast access: Faster than DSL and dial-up services with speeds of up to 25 Mbps and 100 Mbps. While satellite internet used to have a reputation for being slow, nowadays it’s possible to enjoy speeds comparable to terrestrial connections.
Constant connectivity: One of the most notable advantages of the satellite dish is its ability to provide a constant and stable connection. Unlike terrestrial connections that can be affected by infrastructure interruptions or adverse weather conditions, satellite internet doesn’t depend on physical cables and relies on satellites in orbit for data transmission. This ensures a reliable and continuous connection, even in areas prone to natural disasters.
High flexibility and mobility: Satellite internet also offers flexibility and mobility. You can have internet access from anywhere covered by the satellite signal, making it an ideal option for people who travel frequently, remote workers, or those who need connectivity in temporary or expanding areas.
No need for a residential phone service: It is not a requirement to have a phone line to access this Internet service.

Disadvantages

High latency →: One of the main disadvantages of the satellite dish is the latency →, that is, the time it takes for the signal to travel from the satellite to Earth. Due to the distance the signal must travel, latency can be higher compared to terrestrial connections. This can affect real-time activities, such as video conferencing or online gaming, where even small delays can be noticeable.
High cost: Satellite internet tends to be more expensive compared to other connectivity options. Service prices are higher than other types of internet, due to the high costs of equipment, operation, and satellites.
Weather conditions: The proper functioning of satellite internet can depend on good weather conditions. For the use of the satellite dish, a clear sky is needed. Signal stability could be compromised by rain or thunderstorms.
Data limitations: Many satellite internet providers apply monthly data caps on their plans. This means that users have a limited amount of data they can download and upload during a given period. If this limit is exceeded, the speed may be reduced or additional charges may apply.




Step 2 → Advantages and disadvantages of the WiMax connection

Advantages

High fluidity and low latency: This allows for a fast and fluid connection with low latency.
No need for a residential phone service: It is not a requirement to have a phone line to access the Internet service.
VoIP calls: There will be companies that, with the installation of this technology, will allow you to make VoIP calls (a technology that allows you to make and receive voice calls over the Internet).

Disadvantages

Direct contact with the repeater is necessary: This means that the antenna you install at your house has to be oriented directly to the site from where the connection is being sent, and if possible, avoiding obstacles that prevent a direct line of sight, such as trees or buildings. This can sometimes make it necessary to install intermediate connection points to bypass obstacles.
Asymmetric speeds: Which means that the download speed will be much higher than the upload speed. WiMAX connections can reach speeds of up to 1Gbps at fixed points, for example, a house, and 365Mbps at mobile points. Even so, it will always depend on what the company you hire for the service offers you.
Traffic congestion: Speed could be affected more easily during peak hours.




Step 3 → Advantages and disadvantages of the Starlink connection

Advantages

Easy installation: The user buys a kit and can set it up autonomously.
High fluidity and low latency: High-speed, low-latency broadband internet. It will have latencies of around 20ms, compared to the average of 600ms.
High flexibility and mobility: Starlink also offers flexibility and mobility. You can have internet access from anywhere covered by the satellite signal, making it an ideal option for people who travel frequently, remote workers, or those who need connectivity in temporary or expanding areas.
Possibility of a full refund of the equipment cost in the first month: If you purchase the service directly from Starlink, there is this possibility: “Try it for 30 days and, if you’re not satisfied, return the equipment and get a full refund,” says Starlink on its website.

Disadvantages

Weather conditions: The proper functioning of satellite internet can depend on good weather conditions. For the use of the satellite dish, a clear sky is needed. Signal stability could be compromised by rain or thunderstorms.
High cost: Starlink’s satellite internet tends to be more expensive compared to other connectivity options. This is due to the high costs associated with launching and maintaining satellites, as well as the infrastructure needed on Earth for the operation of ground stations. The cost of this service is 300,000 COP** per month with a one-time payment for the equipment of **1,900,000 COP.
Capacity limitations: Since the Starlink system relies on satellites in low orbit, capacity is limited and shared among users in a given area. In congested areas, this could result in reduced speed during peak hours.
Interference problems: Some reports suggest that Starlink can experience interference problems, especially in densely populated areas or regions with high satellite activity.
Environmental impact: The deployment of thousands of satellites in low orbit has raised concerns about the environmental impact and the generation of space debris.
Need for direct view of the sky: To use Starlink, it is necessary to have a direct view of the sky, which can limit its viability in areas with significant obstructions like tall trees or buildings.




Step 4 → How to choose the best option for my community?

Now that you have a clearer idea of what each of the three options consists of, their advantages and disadvantages, you can make a more informed decision together with your community. We consider the following to be important elements when choosing an option:


Availability
Although we did this analysis in 2024 for Colombia, it can be useful for other countries. However, the first thing is to contact the companies that offer internet services in your region; they will be able to guide you better and tell you if they offer WiMax technology. But remember, their interest is to sell, but you are the one who decides. Satellite internet and Starlink have global coverage, so they won’t depend exclusively on the providers in your region.


Budget
First of all, define what your budget will be; for this, you can calculate how many days of work you are willing to invest together with your community to hire this service. Don’t go into debt for an internet plan!



Photo: Maxi Gagliano - Pexels


Reliability
It is important to know if the company you selected has a good reputation or not. You can find this out from other users who have hired them, and it will be vital when you have any inconvenience or have to do any kind of equipment maintenance.


Usage habits
Depending on what your community uses the internet for, you can choose a technology that benefits you more. Here you can evaluate if latency is important because you need to make video calls or play online, if you are willing to hire a monthly paid service, or simply, since the use is occasional, you only pay for the internet service in the months of greatest use, or if, simply, these options are not the most suitable and you prefer to continue without an internet connection.



Don’t get fooled
Define your usage and number of devices to estimate the speed and Bandwidth → needed, and then evaluate the available technology (satellite is a common option) and the reliability and technical support of the provider.
Research the provider’s reputation with neighbors and ask if they offer specific plans for rural areas. The upload speed, download speed, and latency must be adequate for your activities, and it is useful to ask about data restrictions and the quality of the provider’s infrastructure.

How much is enough?
One of these three solutions might be the right one to solve connectivity in your region, because they are all designed for places far from cities and do not depend on a wired internet service for their operation.
You can keep the following criteria in mind and think about them in terms of the people and the content you need to access:

For basic use (emails, social networks, browsing): A moderate download speed and a basic data plan might be enough.
For streaming and online work: A higher download speed and greater bandwidth are required to avoid interruptions.
For intensive upload use (cloud, large files): It is important to look for a symmetric connection, where the upload speed is close to the download speed.

en/solve/solv-choose-satellite-internet.summary: Don't throw your money away; choose the right satellite internet for your needs.
en/solve/solv-choose-satellite-internet.content:
Hi, I’m Nicolás, and just like you, I’ve been learning how to improve my internet connection. I’m no expert, but by searching around, following tutorials, and learning through trial and error, I’ve worked on improving internet quality in places that don’t have great connectivity.
In this specific solution, we’ll figure out the criteria for choosing which satellite internet best fits our connectivity needs. We’ll also face some ethical questions that might influence our choice.
Our advice: decide with both your head and your heart, choosing the option that best serves your needs and those of your community.
What does it mean to choose satellite internet with criteria?
Satellite internet is a technology designed so that the internet signal is sent via a satellite in orbit to the satellite dish at your home or business.
With satellite internet, you can connect computers, cell phones →, tablets, etc. This technology doesn’t need the cabling used by, for example, fiber optic internet.

What is it for?
This solution is here to help you decide which satellite internet is best for you to buy if you’re located in a place without an internet connection.
In this solution, we’ll cover the pros and cons of three different solutions so you can make a conscious and responsible decision: satellite dish, WiMax, or Starlink.
Before you start, we suggest that if you decide to buy any of the options presented in this solution, you could pay for it together with other people and enjoy community use of the internet.

Before we start, some ethical questions
Do you think everyone, regardless of where they are, should have access to the internet? In Colombia, for example, a 2021 legislative act established and elevated the internet to a fundamental right, making it an obligation to expand internet coverage to unconnected communities and territories. For their part, international organizations like the UN state that denying access to the Internet is like denying the right to freedom of expression.
This might sound great, but the reality is complex and unequal. On one hand, not everyone and every community has the internet: nearly a third of the world’s population remains without an internet connection—about 2.6 billion people. Internet service providers aren’t keen on reaching places where there’s no infrastructure, as the profit potential is lower. This widens and maintains the inequity regarding internet access. On the other hand, the deployment of thousands of satellites in low earth orbit has raised concerns about environmental impact and the generation of space junk.
So, at SOLE Colombia, we see satellite internet as one of the existing options, especially designed for places that don’t have an internet connection or nearby telecommunications towers to distribute it. If this isn’t your case, perhaps you can find a more conscious solution tailored to your needs in the content of this guide.

How do I know if I need this solution?
Before we start, we’d like to ask you a few questions:

Do you currently have fair or good quality fiber optic or mobile internet?
Where you live, can you see telecommunications towers distributing internet?
Are there companies that can offer you an internet service at a good price?

If your answer was yes to any of these questions, we recommend you stick with your mobile or fiber optic internet and look for other solutions on SOLE Voltaje → that might help you improve your connection. But don’t go yet! We invite you to keep reading this guide so you can learn more about satellite internet and make your own decisions.
If, on the other hand, you answered “no” to all the previous questions, you have a poor internet connection, and you’ve already checked other solutions, we invite you to keep reading this solution.

Options to review
In this solution, we’ll work with three technologies available in Colombia: Satellite internet, WiMax, and Starlink for the year 2024. The estimated reading time for this solution is about 15 minutes, but don’t be scared; you can read these recommendations with the help of others. Remember that at SOLE Voltaje, we want to promote the collective use of the internet.

Satellite internet
The most popular internet option in rural areas is satellite internet. Although the name explains itself, it’s about connecting to the internet via satellites. The great advantage of this option is that it can reach anywhere, including the most remote rural areas! To access this technology, the company will need to install a satellite dish at your home.



WiMax
How WiMAX works is simple, as it’s a repeater from the company you want to hire, emitting microwave signals that reach your antenna. Therefore, the first thing you need is to contact a company that offers these services and has a repeater near your house to send you the signal. Then, you have to put an antenna on the facade of your house. This antenna will have to point directly at the service provider’s repeater or an intermediate connection point used to bypass obstacles between your antenna and their repeater. The antenna installation will be done by the company itself.


_Image taken from Wikipedia

Starlink
Starlink is Elon Musk’s satellite internet project. It’s a specific type of satellite internet that facilitates connections, especially in rural areas. The company is considered the first and largest satellite constellation in the world that uses low earth orbit to offer broadband, high-speed, and low-latency satellite internet. This allows for streaming content, online gaming, video calls, and more.

To get it up and running, the user buys a kit with everything needed, most notably the antenna, which must be placed outside and automatically orients itself to establish a connection in a matter of minutes, provided it has a clear view of the sky.

_Image taken from Starlink

We’ve got an introduction to the available options; now let’s get to the moment where we want you to know the criteria you should keep in mind to choose the option that suits you best.

What should I keep in mind to make this decision?
Availability: Are these options available for where I live?
Although we did this analysis in 2024 for Colombia, it can be useful for other countries. To know the availability of these three options, you must keep in mind that, unlike WiMax, satellite internet and Starlink have global coverage, so they won’t depend exclusively on the providers in your region. For the WiMax option, the first thing you should do is contact the companies that offer internet services in your region; they will be able to guide you and tell you if they actually offer this technology.
Budget: How much money can I pay?

The cost of WiMax service can start from 150,000 COP** per month with a payment for the equipment between **300,000 COP and $2,000,000 COP, depending on the company you want to hire.
The cost of satellite internet service can start from 150,000 COP** per month with a payment for the equipment between **300,000 COP and $2,000,000 COP, depending on the company you want to hire.
The cost of Starlink service can start from 180,000 COP** per month with a one-time payment for the equipment of **1,900,000 COP.

Weather conditions: Can the weather affect the internet signal?

For Starlink and satellite internet, the quality of the internet will depend on weather conditions. For the use of a satellite dish, a clear sky is needed; for this reason, signal stability could be compromised by rain or thunderstorms.
For WiMax, keep in mind that direct contact with the repeater is necessary; this means that the antenna you install at your house has to be oriented directly to the site where the connection is being sent, and if possible, avoiding obstacles that block the direct line of sight, such as trees or buildings. Sometimes it may be necessary to install intermediate connection points to bypass obstacles.

Signal and coverage: Which option offers me the best quality?

The advantage of satellite internet is that it has global coverage, which means that people living in remote regions or rural areas can access the Internet reliably. One of the most notable advantages of satellite internet is its ability to provide a constant and stable connection. Unlike terrestrial connections that can be affected by infrastructure interruptions or adverse weather conditions, satellite internet doesn’t depend on cables. This guarantees a reliable and continuous connection, even in areas prone to natural disasters.
Now, the disadvantage of satellite internet is that many providers offer a limited amount of data that can be downloaded and uploaded during a certain period. If this limit is exceeded, the speed may be reduced, or additional charges may apply.
For WiMax, the advantage is that you don’t need a residential telephone service. It’s not a requirement to have a landline to access the Internet service.
Now, a disadvantage is that the download internet speed will be much higher than the upload speed. WiMAX connections can reach speeds of up to 1Gbps at fixed points, for example, a house, and 365Mbps at mobile points. Even so, it will always depend on what the company you hire offers you. Keep in mind, also, that the speed could be affected more easily during peak hours.
For its part, Starlink offers an easy installation that you and your community can carry out: the company offers the user a kit with the necessary instructions to assemble it. Starlink also offers flexibility and mobility. You can have Internet access from anywhere covered by the satellite signal, which makes it an ideal option for people who travel frequently, remote workers, or those who need connectivity in temporary or expanding areas.
Now, since the Starlink system is based on satellites in low orbit, capacity is limited and shared among users in a given area. In congested areas, this could result in reduced speed during peak hours, although its coverage is improving more and more. Some reports suggest that Starlink can experience interference issues, especially in densely populated areas or regions with high satellite activity. For this reason, keep in mind that to use Starlink, it’s necessary to have a direct view of the sky, which can limit its viability in areas with significant obstructions like tall trees or buildings.

What signal speed do I need?
By latency →, we refer to the time it takes for the signal to travel from the satellite to Earth. For Starlink, the broadband Internet is high-speed and low-latency. It will have latencies of around 20ms, compared to the average of 600ms.
For its part, WiMax allows for a fast and fluid connection with low latencies.
Now, the speed of satellite internet can be lower compared to terrestrial connections. This can affect real-time activities, such as video conferencing or online gaming, where even small delays can be noticeable.

en/solve/solv-community-meeting-space.title: How to snag a community hall or any shared space to get online together?
en/solve/solv-community-meeting-space.summary: Public spaces belong to everyone, let's put them to work!
en/solve/solv-community-meeting-space.content:
Hi, I’m Manu. As a SOLE Explorer, I’ve had to learn how to request community spaces in the places where we’ve gone to run SOLE, and I know it’s not always easy to know where to start.

What does it mean to ask for a community hall, or any community space?
This is a solution that guides you on how to book a common space to use the Internet as a group, or for whatever else you want to do in that space. Remember that every space has its own rules and request procedures, so this solution can guide you on the criteria, but it’s not a definitive solution.
If you have any suggestions on how you do it in your community that you think might help others, I invite you to comment on the solution—we create the Internet together!

What is it for?
At SOLE Colombia, we believe it’s more fun when we do things together. Community halls are spaces for us to meet others, to connect, to celebrate, to share, and you can use them too.
Here I’ll tell you some steps you can follow to book the community hall closest to you. Good luck!

What do you need?

A good attitude, believe in yourself.
An ID document to sign the booking (optional).
A letter to request the space booking (optional).


How to do it?

Step 1 → Discover the place and head over there

Once you decide where you want to carry out your activity, go to the community hall and talk to the people in charge.
Introduce yourself and tell them why you want to use the space, what for, and how many people have confirmed.
Encourage them to participate in your activity too; for example, if you are going to do a SOLE, you can invite them to become participants.



Step 2 → Ask about the necessary requirements


Once you are in contact with the people in charge, ask them about availability and what requirements you need, or how you can book it.


Step 3 → Write the booking letter or meet the place’s requirements

Usually, community halls require a letter to book the space.
Write down what the activity will consist of, when it will take place, and who the organizers and participants will be.
Also, it is very important that you include your contact details; they will need them to confirm if it’s possible for your activity to take place at the time you have planned.
We also advise you to include a few words of thanks for the authorization to use the space.
You may need to attach a photocopy of your ID, so keep that in mind.
Do you think an example could help you? Here are the steps to keep in mind and what the example would look like:

Include the place and date where you are.
Address the letter to the name or title of the person, or entity, that owns or manages the space.
Introduce yourself as the person responsible for the request or the organization of the activity.
Explain the purpose of the activity and its details. You can also request items you need to carry out your activity, for example, chairs, tables, computers, or other items you require that are available to whoever is lending you the hall.
Thank them for their attention and let them know how they can respond to you. It could be your phone number or another way to contact you.
Finally, sign the letter.

This is what this formula would look like written out:


💡 El Montecillo Neighborhood
Arracachal Municipality
February 13, 2038
Good morning,
My name is (your full name), I am identified with ID No. (ID Number), and I am contacting you to request the use of the (name of the space or meeting hall) to carry out an activity, in the company of people from the community.
My idea is to use the space to learn, dialogue, and solve some challenges in my community that we will identify in the meeting, using the Internet as a group.
The meeting details are:

Date: (day of the week), (day) of (month) of (year)
Time: at (time)
Number of people: we will meet (number) people
Duration of the meeting: (time)

To carry out the activity, we need some conditions and furniture: one chair per person, some tables where we can place some computers, and the possibility to plug them in (so they don’t run out of battery). It is also necessary to have electricity and an Internet connection available.
We commit to taking care of the common space and complying with the rules of use in this space for everyone.
You can contact me at (phone number) or through (other contact method).
Thank you very much for your attention, I look forward to hearing from you.
(Name of the person signing).



Remember that this is just an example; you can draft the letter however you like. Don’t forget to ask the person in charge what information, data, or attachments you need to include in the document.


Step 4 → Ask for a contact for follow-up

It may happen that your confirmation needs to go through some filters or that the process takes a while. Although you shouldn’t lose your cool, it doesn’t hurt to ask for the contact details of the person to follow up on the process; this way, you’ll ensure you can plan and make your activity a reality within the deadlines you had in mind.


Step 5 → Thank them for the help and celebrate

Once they confirm you can use the space, don’t forget to thank the person in charge with whom you were in contact from the beginning.
You can send them an email, a WhatsApp message, or greet them on the street, reminding them how important their support was in making the activity happen. They are a good ally for future occasions when you want to use the community hall again.

You can share your experience booking the community hall in your neighborhood, community, or complex with others :) Remember that learning in a group is very powerful, and your experience can help or inspire others!

How to know if this solution works?
The moment you have your space booked, it’s just a matter of iterating the process as many times as you need. Perhaps you can make a broader request that lasts longer. For this, it can be useful to leverage the good news, findings, and successes of the activity you have proposed in the space and how it is bearing fruit in the community.
For example, when you manage to get a group of people to do SOLE recurrently, you will be able to verify the benefits it has for skills like communication, negotiation, reading comprehension, digital competencies, autonomy, leadership… making a small report, for example, with the result of the Reflection capsules (available on the SOLE Colombia website n9.cl/reflexionatusole), can be very powerful to strengthen the relationship with your ally and with the people in your community.

Other possible Internets
Sometimes, the paperwork involving large entities, or that involves the decision of many people, can take time. It is important that, at the time of the request, you are clear about the deadlines and can set reminders to follow up on your request.
Often it is enough to remind the person with whom you made the request, stop by to say hello kindly, and remind them that you are waiting for an answer. They will appreciate your attention and will surely put more effort into having an answer for you.

en/solve/solv-create-poweful-message.title: How to rally others to your cause?
en/solve/solv-create-poweful-message.summary: Craft a punchy message so folks can really connect with your purpose.
en/solve/solv-create-poweful-message.content:
Hi! I’m Manu, the storyteller here at SOLE Colombia, and today I want to talk to you about the power of a message.
If you’re here, it’s because you want to learn how to rally others around your cause and build a powerful message. Shall we do it together?
What does it mean to create a powerful message?
In this solution, we’re going to dive into a very special methodology in the world of storytelling: the Golden Circle, created by Simon Sinek. We’ll use this step-by-step method to help you develop a clear and powerful message.
Through the three fundamental questions Sinek poses, I’ll guide you to unravel the message behind your cause. When you rally others with a clear and powerful message, you make them feel deeply connected to you.
Get ready, because this is going to be exciting!

What is it for?
Creating a powerful message, focused on your purpose, means connecting emotionally with your audience and inspiring them to take action. It’s used to inspire others, appealing to their emotions and values to create a deeper, more meaningful connection. You’ll create communication that is more coherent and consistent.

What do you need?

Paper.
A pen/pencil or any digital tool.
And, of course, enthusiasm.


How to do it?
.mp4?table=block&id=12a2bd68-c5b6-81cc-a580-d32a8d9dbe02&spaceId=d2a8cf29-6055-4dd9-8971-801014f46b2a&expirationTimestamp=1763841600000&signature=t7dES7O4_HiGNKUqaCTIdIWssmujJ57DJJfJZl-zgUM&downloadName=V%C3%ADdeo+sin+t%C3%ADtulo+%E2%80%90+Hecho+con+Clipchamp+%285%29.mp4)

Step 1 → Start with the “what”

What is it that you do or want to do? What do you want to share or offer the world? That is the “what” of your message. Starting with the “what” will help you glimpse your “why” more easily.
Here, your ideas take shape and turn into tangible actions: a product, a service, or an offer.
Activity: To discover it, I invite you to write down on a blank sheet of paper what you are doing or offering in tangible terms… A SOLE?, an activity?, a product?
If you still have doubts, use the examples to start your golden circle. Go for it!
.mp4?table=block&id=12a2bd68-c5b6-814d-842d-ed4a523d2e50&spaceId=d2a8cf29-6055-4dd9-8971-801014f46b2a&expirationTimestamp=1763841600000&signature=qsuMcmRXv2dcQh07g-Vprno0Hd-gVfQ4Q9J8TvazBkM&downloadName=V%C3%ADdeo+sin+t%C3%ADtulo+%E2%80%90+Hecho+con+Clipchamp+%286%29.mp4)

Step 2 → Define the “how”

We’re on the right track! With the purpose clear, everything else falls into place… Now that you know that flame that drives you, it’s time to think about how to fuel it and bring your message to the world. What strategies, actions, or methods will you use to make your “why” shine?
The time has come to determine the methods and processes you will use to carry out your “what.” For this step, you need to know how you do what you do to fulfill your motivation. Think about whether it’s a format that makes you unique, a product no one else had thought of, or an original service you offer. What matters here are the qualities.
Activity:

Write a list on a sheet of paper of the activities you do to fulfill your “what” and select the ones you find most relevant.
Now put them all in the same place and draft your “how.”

See how I did it to guide you:
.mp4?table=block&id=12a2bd68-c5b6-8192-8f51-e483e5a18759&spaceId=d2a8cf29-6055-4dd9-8971-801014f46b2a&expirationTimestamp=1763841600000&signature=21nStT-wV9899mSVRyYiM3TwfExlRiAXYCOyQrQsUp4&downloadName=V%C3%ADdeo+sin+t%C3%ADtulo+%E2%80%90+Hecho+con+Clipchamp+%287%29.mp4)


Step 3 → Give shape to your “why”

To finish, it’s necessary that you have a clear understanding of the fundamental purpose behind the message. What is the inspiring reason that motivates you?
When we are clear about our “why,” we create an emotional bond with our audience, sparking their interest and commitment on a deeper level.
Activity: To discover the “why” of your message, grab a blank sheet of paper and write down the first thing that comes to your head. Don’t overthink it. It’s okay if it’s just a few words; little by little, they will take shape 😉 Here is how my “why” turned out:
.mp4?table=block&id=12a2bd68-c5b6-8100-9062-c2b1908a766d&spaceId=d2a8cf29-6055-4dd9-8971-801014f46b2a&expirationTimestamp=1763841600000&signature=ELqQzigFtqRvfID_QQZP9O9gf7MzlJ9aQMRxAnvjzK8&downloadName=V%C3%ADdeo+sin+t%C3%ADtulo+%E2%80%90+Hecho+con+Clipchamp+%288%29.mp4)
Tip: Think about what motivates you to do what you’re doing, and you’ll see that the words will appear little by little.

How do you know if this solution works?
There you have it; your “why” is ready, and now your message is much more powerful. You can now have more clarity when you want to spread your purpose or that of your product to others. Remember, the most important thing is that it’s authentic, that it reflects your essence, and that it makes you feel identified.
Now it’s your time to shine! Go ahead, conquer the world with your message! 🚀 Show us in the comments what your Golden Circle looks like!

Other possible Internets
Your message should reflect your purpose, that which drives you to action. It must be authentic and resonate with the people listening to you.
Aligning your messages and your actions with your purpose makes your communication coherent; take care of it. If your message is genuine, authentic, and reflects your true passion, you will be honoring your “why.”
It is very important that your message creates an emotional connection with whoever receives it; remember that only when we create emotional bonds with others do we manage to make our words truly touch their hearts.
Remember! The goal of a powerful message is to motivate others to do something, to take action, and to follow you, be inspired, connect, and be motivated to follow your vision.

en/solve/solv-debian-thinkpad-server.title: How to build a robust Debian server on a ThinkPad laptop?
en/solve/solv-debian-thinkpad-server.summary: Install Debian 13 on a laptop to build a solid, efficient server that never sleeps.
en/solve/solv-debian-thinkpad-server.content:
Hi! I’m David. I’ve managed to improve the stability of our SOLE labs through trial and error. At first, I used computers with Windows or heavy versions of Linux, but I discovered that for a server to run for months without shutting down, the best thing is to use Debian without a graphical interface.
This guide was born from the need to take advantage of powerful laptops like the ThinkPad T480s to make them the heart of a SOLE Lab. I’m no expert, but after wrestling with the BIOS and user permissions, here is the method that worked for me to have a robust system.

What is a robust server with Debian?
It’s turning a computer (in this case, a ThinkPad laptop) into a machine dedicated exclusively to providing services to others, like files or web pages. By installing Debian 13 “clean” (without a desktop), the equipment uses very little energy and RAM, leaving all its power for what really matters: the community.

What is it for?
It’s useful for having an information hub that is always on. By using a laptop, we have a huge advantage: the battery acts as a backup (UPS) if the power goes out. Plus, being a robust installation, it’s much harder for the system to break or freeze due to visual software errors.

Before you start…

Heads up: Installing this system will erase all files on the computer. Make sure to back up anything you need before continuing.
Tip: For this installation, we will use the Medicat tool, which is like a Swiss Army knife on a USB drive.


What do you need?

A ThinkPad laptop (or similar) with its charger.
A USB drive with Medicat installed.
A wired internet connection (preferably) to download the packages.
Curiosity and the willingness to type a few commands.


How to do it?
Preparing the ground (BIOS)

Step 1 → Disable Secure Boot

Modern laptops come with a lock called Secure Boot that sometimes prevents tools like Medicat from booting.

Restart the computer and repeatedly press the F1 key (or Enter and then F1) to enter the BIOS.
Look for the Security tab and enter Secure Boot.
Change the option to Disabled.
Press F10 to save and exit.


You’re on the right track: If you press F12 upon restarting and see your USB drive in the list, you’ve already cleared the first hurdle.


Installing Debian 13

Step 2 → Start the graphical installer

Boot from the USB and choose Graphical Install. It’s more comfortable for configuring the network and the disk.

Language: Choose your language, but double-check that the keyboard layout matches what you see on your keys (usually Latin American Spanish or your local standard).
Network: Give the computer a short name (e.g., sole-server).
Users: This is key. It will ask for a “root” (administrator) password and then to create a normal user.

We recommend the user: sole-s or soles.
Password example: SOLE123 (But change it to a secure one and keep it safe!).




Heads up: If you leave the root password blank, your normal user will be able to use the ‘sudo’ command automatically. If you set a root password, you will have to configure ‘sudo’ manually later (see Step 5).



Step 3 → Select software (Critical Point)

For the server to be robust and lightweight, on the “Software selection” screen:

UNCHECK: “Debian desktop environment” and “GNOME” (we don’t want a desktop).
CHECK: “SSH server” (to manage it from another PC).
CHECK: “Standard system utilities”.



Laptop configuration (Don’t let it sleep)

Step 4 → Configure lid closing

By default, a laptop turns off or goes to sleep when you close the lid. We want the server to keep running even if it’s closed.

Enter the terminal and type:
sudo nano /etc/systemd/logind.conf
Look for these lines and remove the # symbol at the beginning, leaving them like this:
HandleLidSwitch=ignore
HandleLidSwitchExternalPower=ignore
HandleLidSwitchDocked=ignore
Save with Ctrl+O, Enter, and exit with Ctrl+X.
Restart the service: sudo systemctl restart systemd-logind.


Keep going: If you get “command not found,” you likely need to fix your user permissions. Check the next step.



Step 5 → Fix the SUDO command (if necessary)

If typing sudo tells you the command is not found, do this:

Type su - and enter the administrator password you chose.
Install sudo: apt update && apt install sudo.
Add your user: usermod -aG sudo soles (change ‘soles’ to your username).
Restart the computer: reboot.



Battery care

Step 6 → Protect the battery with TLP

Since the laptop will be plugged in almost all the time, the battery can suffer. We will install a tool so it doesn’t always charge to 100%.

Install TLP: sudo apt update && apt install tlp.
Configure the limits (e.g., start charging at 40% and stop at 80%):
sudo tlp setcharge 40 80


Food for thought: This extends the life of your equipment by years, preventing the battery from swelling or getting damaged by heat.



How do you know if this solution works?

Close the laptop lid. If you can still log in from another computer via SSH or if the web server is still responding, you did it!
The equipment should feel cool and quiet, since having no graphical interface consumes very few resources.


Recommendations

Always use a static IP so it’s easy to find the server on the network.
Clean the dust from the laptop fan before leaving it on 24/7.
Keep the passwords on a piece of paper inside the SOLE Lab or in a secure manager.


Other possible internets
Having a robust server is like having a library that never closes. You can install a Pocket Wikipedia or a file system so the kids in the SOLE can save their work without fear of it being deleted.

Related solutions
This guide is the solid foundation for then applying these others:

The next level is installing applications: How to create your own Pocket Server?
If the equipment is very old and you prefer something visual: Second life for an old computer with Linux
To understand what’s inside your server: How to know how much RAM I have?

en/solve/solv-discover-audience.title: How to reach the people who will value your message most?
en/solve/solv-discover-audience.summary: Find out who your audience is.
en/solve/solv-discover-audience.content:
Hi there! 😊
I’m Manu, and I was a storyteller at SOLE Colombia for several years. I always keep in mind who I’m talking to… have you ever wondered how to really reach the people who will value your message the most?
In this solution, we’re going to figure out your audience together. Ready to roll up your sleeves?

What is discovering your audience?
Knowing your audience means deeply understanding the folks you’re aiming your content at. When you know your audience, you can focus your efforts where you know they’ll make a splash.
Knowing your audience is like knowing the shortcut to get straight to the heart of your community and connect with the right people.

What’s it for?
When you know who you’re talking to, you can tweak your message, tone, and style so it really resonates with them.
You’ll improve how they see you, but more importantly, you’ll be able to build genuine connections because your message will hit home.

What do you need?

Paper
Pen or pencil
Enthusiasm
Smartphone or computer


How to do it?

Step 1 → Define your target audience

Figure out who you want to reach. Think about the key traits. Jot down on a sheet of paper: What are their interests? What challenges are they facing?


Step 2 → Create your personas

Create detailed profiles. Write down their basic qualities (age, location), what motivates them, and where they usually hang out. This will help you better visualize who you’re talking to.


Step 3 → Observe and listen to your folks

Start interacting with your audience through surveys or just by watching their interactions online. Note down any responses or patterns that help you understand them better.


How do you know if this solution is working?
Watch how the people who interact with your messages behave. If you notice that folks are responding more or feeling more identified with what you’re saying, you’re hitting the mark!

Other possible Internets
As you get better at defining your audience, you’ll realize there are subgroups that need different messages. At SOLE, we talk to Grandmas and Tech-Tinkerers in different ways, but always with the same care.

en/solve/solv-donated-equipment.title: How to score donated gear?
en/solve/solv-donated-equipment.summary: Giving a second life to equipment that would otherwise end up in the trash.
en/solve/solv-donated-equipment.content:
Hey, are you there? My name is Mateo, and I’ll be your guide as you develop this solution. If you’re reading, listening to, or watching this, it’s because you’re interested or curious about how to get donated equipment. If that’s the case, you’re in the right place.

What is getting donated equipment?
In a nutshell, this solution is about reuse. It’s about being consistent with caring for the world we live in; it’s about making the most of things that are obsolete to others but that we might be able to use for a long time to come.
This solution is for giving a second chance to equipment that is no longer needed. Did you know there are companies looking to upgrade their gear and donate what they have? This equipment is usually in good condition, and your community could put it to good use.

What is this solution for?
While this solution doesn’t require money to buy equipment, keep in mind that it can take weeks, or even months, depending on the steps we’ll walk you through below. That said, you have a better chance of receiving a donation if you can demonstrate that the equipment will be used for community purposes and that its goal is to improve people’s quality of life.

What do you need?

Persistence.
Patience.
Support from others. Teamwork increases your chances of making it happen.


How to do it?
Let’s get started!
This solution unfolds in three steps where we’ll share everything we know and have learned at Fundación SOLE Colombia about how to get donated equipment. Every case is different, so it’s important that you’re willing to adapt these steps based on the hurdles you find along the way.

Photo: veerasak Piyawatanakul - Pexels


Step 1 → Find the donor company and identify the relationship model
Generally, equipment donors are companies with significant financial capacity, payroll, and infrastructure. Think of phone or computer companies, universities, or look into the sponsors of social projects in your region. That said, we suggest starting with smaller companies. You have two options for this:

Option 1: Direct search

You can look for companies or individuals who donate equipment via the internet, social media, or by checking with your network of contacts and close circles.

💬 For option 1, make a list of companies and the ways you can contact them—it could be through the people who handle the organization’s finances or those who manage the computer equipment.
The key is to get a direct contact at the donor company with whom you can speak in person, send an email, make a call, or send a letter. If you send a letter or email, make sure it will be read, and if they aren’t the person responsible for making that decision, ensure they will redirect it to the person you need.


Option 2: Outreach

You can write a post or announcement on social media making it clear that: 1. you need donated equipment in good condition; 2. you have a community project where many people will benefit; 3. include a number where they can contact you; 4. be clear about who you are and try to make the message spark empathy and trust. An example message could be:

“Hi everyone! My name is Amaranta and I’m part of the XYZ FOUNDATION. Does anyone know of organizations that are donating computer equipment in good condition? We’re looking for support to implement a project with seniors in rural areas of Colombia. Any information or contact would be a huge help. Thanks!
My contact number is 123456789
We suggest doing both options at the same time; this will broaden your chances of finding a donor company.


💪🏽 Keep it up! At this point, it’s key to be persistent. There’s no magic formula; it’s a matter of knocking on doors and paving the way. In any case, if you’ve read this far, it’s because you already have the will to do it, and that’s something to admire.




Step 2 → Wait for a response and don’t let the contact “go cold.”


Photo by Fauxels: Pexels
Once you’ve sent the requests, all that’s left is to wait and follow up continuously to get a response. Don’t let the contact go cold; if more than a week passes without a response, write again or go in person if possible. When you get an affirmative response, be clear about the model under which you will receive the equipment: not all companies donate their equipment; some decide to give it away as a gift. There are two types of models:


Option 1: Gifting equipment

You might find a company or person who is just giving their equipment away. Family members might give away equipment. When you contact them, make sure you understand the terms under which you will actually receive the equipment.


Option 2: Donating equipment

Now, for companies that donate, it’s a different model where a second chance is given to equipment that is in good condition and can be used by people and communities who need it.
How does it work? Many companies have to perform upgrades that require changing their equipment or they need new technology to carry out their work, so they decide to donate, which allows them to receive a tax deduction.

⚠️ Keep in mind that for this to be possible, donor companies need to receive a donation certificate. If you aren’t part of a foundation, you must find an ally who can issue this certificate for you.

Who issues this certificate for companies that want to donate, and how? To find an ally, think of a non-profit entity that has an active legal status and can issue these certificates for the companies that will donate the equipment. For example, foundations, cooperatives, or similar entities in your region. Talk to them and tell them about your purpose. If they decide to support you, ask them for guidance in this process.
We invite you to look up the story of Alex Cortés, an engineer who founded Fundación Click → with the goal of giving a second life to computers that many people, organizations, or companies no longer need; he decides to repair them, perform maintenance, and give them away or donate them to those who need them most. If you want to know more about his story, we invite you to look him up, his foundation, and his history.

⚠️⚠️ Important: You must be clear about how the equipment will be used, as legally the equipment will belong to the ally you found. Don’t forget to check that the equipment they give you is functional. We don’t want you to end up storing electronic waste that you’ll have to repair.



Step 3 → Receiving the equipment and building the relationship


Photo: Ketut Subiyanto - Pexels

Photo: Cytonn photography - Pexels
For receiving the equipment, in either of the two models, keep in mind that each company or person has their own procedure.
The delivery of the equipment might be a shipment, or you might have to pick it up or reach an agreement on the delivery location with the company or person making the donation. After delivery, it’s important to know what kind of relationship you want and can build with them:


Option 1: Gifting equipment

In this model, paperwork is usually not required to formalize the delivery. However, it’s likely that the donors will want to establish a short- or medium-term relationship to know the destination and use of the equipment. If this is your case, we suggest making it explicit and maintaining cordial communication with them.

For example, although it is not mandatory, at Fundación SOLE Colombia, we usually formalize the process through a thank-you letter signed by both parties, where the delivery, the condition of the equipment, and our commitment to put them to good use are corroborated.



Option 2: Donating equipment

For the delivery, make a donation request explaining your interests, conditions, and the cooperation you will build.
How many computers do you need? What condition is the equipment you are going to receive in? What does the donor company need from you? What will you use the equipment for? Who will be the people and communities benefiting? For this option, we suggest that, just like in option 1, you consider the possibility of building a bond with the donor company.

At SOLE Colombia, we usually send the donor companies photographs that thank them and show the community use of the equipment, with which we try to open the possibilities for future donations.


What does community use of equipment imply?
Do you remember what we mentioned at the beginning of this solution about the chances you might have of receiving a donation if you demonstrate that the equipment use will be community-based? Now we invite you to reflect on the importance that collective use of equipment can have in a community. It’s not just about receiving them, but about reaching agreements on who will manage them, how they will be used, and how often; this will involve fostering dialogue and teamwork. It’s not about having a lot of equipment, but about knowing how to use it as a community.

See you soon! We invite you to investigate other solutions and keep tinkering.


How to know if this solution works?
When you receive equipment that others aren’t using, you’ve proven that this solution works. You will also have created a relationship with someone; that’s beautiful and powerful. Someone who has tuned into your purpose and wants to lend you a hand.
As you create new relationships, you will feel more and more confident in finding potential donors. Now that you have equipment, would you be up for trying another solution? Browse more Voltaje solutions →

Other possible Internets
When you cultivate the relationship with your donors, it’s possible they might make donations more than once. Can you imagine if they donated a few computers to you every year? What would you do then with all that equipment?

If you want to know what we do at SOLE Colombia with the computers donated to us, take a look at www.solecolombia.org

Thinking about how you can extend this benefit to others is a way of making this world a fairer place. Would you like to try it in your community? Was this solution useful to you? We hope so! And if it was, share it with other people who you know could use it.
See you soon! 👋🏽

Having community computers brings new challenges: How to share available computers?
If electricity in your community is unstable or non-existent, you can check out this alternative: How to generate electricity using a bicycle?
When you have equipment and electricity, it’s time to get connected. There are several options. This is one of them: 4G antenna?

en/solve/solv-endless.title: A slice of the Internet on offline computers
en/solve/solv-endless.content:
📄 View video summary (Accessibility)
  
    This video serves as a companion guide for learning how to install Endless OS on computers without an Internet connection. The tutorial explains the technical process needed to implement this educational tool in offline environments.
  


If you’re reading this, it’s because you like to “tinker” with computers to make them do more than just write documents in Word. Installing Endless OS is like stuffing a giant library into a computer, whether it’s old or new.

What is this solution for?
Endless OS is an Operating System designed to work where internet is scarce. It comes with Wikipedia, courses, and educational games already downloaded. It lets kids look for answers to their Big Questions even if the router is turned off.

What do you need for this mission?

A computer with Windows.
Internet connection (only for the initial download).
A USB flash drive of at least 32GB.
At least 32GB of free space on the computer.
Plenty of patience.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Do an initial check
Check if the computer has enough space. In Windows, open the file explorer and make sure the “C: Drive” has at least 32GB free.

Tip: If the internet is slow, use a download manager so you don’t lose progress if the connection drops.




Step 2 → Download the installer
Go to the official Endless site and choose:

Windows Installer: Creates an automatic dual-boot (you can choose between Windows or Endless when turning it on).
ISO Image: For advanced users who want to format the machine.





Step 3 → Run the installation
If you use the Windows installer, double-click it and select “Install alongside Windows”. Choose the “Full” version, which is the one that comes with all the educational content.

Heads up: If it looks like it’s stuck at 99%, don’t turn it off. It’s moving heavy files.




Step 4 → Configure the boot (BIOS)
If you are using a USB drive and the PC doesn’t boot from it, press F2 or F12 when turning it on to enter the BIOS. Look for the “Boot” tab and put the USB first in the list.



Collective Glossary

Operating System: The main program that makes the computer work.
ISO Image: A file that contains the entire system packaged together.
Bootable USB: A memory stick prepared to start an operating system.


Final recommendations

Update before you go: Let the system update while you still have internet.
Test the search: Make sure the articles load correctly offline.

en/solve/solv-express-invite.title: Learn to design an express invitation without being an expert!
en/solve/solv-express-invite.summary: Invitations are key to rallying people.
en/solve/solv-express-invite.content:
Hi there! I’m Manuela. I love designing, drawing, and creating. Today, I’d like to share how to make an invitation based on my own tinkering. Here, I’ll focus mainly on the form. You can also check out How to write a good invitation? for tips on the content.

What does designing an invitation mean?
Designing an invitation is all about picking the right graphic elements (colors, images, fonts) to make your message pop and grab attention. Invitations can be handmade or digital.

What’s it for?
An invitation is for rallying the troops. It’s the first point of contact we have with people and the best chance to hook them into our activities.

What do you need?

A computer or smartphone with internet (for digital).
Paper, colors, and markers (for analog).
A dash of creativity and the freedom to express yourself.


How to do it?
Your handmade invitation

Step 1 → Pick your colors

Use colored paper and bring it to life with pencils or markers. Add decorative borders or symbols that represent your event.


Step 2 → Write the essential text

Make sure the details are easy to read. Be creative but clear. Remember that “less is more”: don’t clutter the invitation.


Step 3 → Review and spread the word

Ask for a second opinion. Check your spelling carefully. If you want to send it via WhatsApp, just snap a high-quality photo of it.

Your digital invitation

Step 4 → Hop into Canva

Open your browser and head over to canva.com. Create a free account with your email.


Step 5 → Choose a size and template

Select the ideal size (postcard or social media). Use the search bar to find a template you like and start tweaking it.


Step 6 → Customize and download

Change the background, add your own photos or icons. When you’re ready, click “Share” and then “Download” as an image (JPG or PNG).


How do you know if this solution works?
Check with someone outside your circle to see if the info is clear (time, place). Go ahead and share it, then see if people are interested in your event.

Heads up: If people don’t show up, it’s not always the invitation’s fault. Check the time, the weather, or the day you picked.
