en/solve/solv-financial-support-connect.summary: Some organizations offer low-cost Internet solutions to get you online.
en/solve/solv-financial-support-connect.content:
Hi, I’m Belén. Although I didn’t write the original version of this solution, I’m reviewing it today so you can get the most out of it. Sometimes we feel like we’re all alone, swimming against the current. I want you to know that it doesn’t have to be that way—there are people and organizations out there who can lend a hand. I hope this solution shows you some paths you can take.
What is seeking financial support in your community to get connected to the Internet?
There are initiatives out there looking to connect people who don’t have internet access, especially in rural, remote, and low-income areas.
They offer funding programs and resources for local communities and organizations that are working on building and expanding internet infrastructure, like community networks and complementary access solutions.
Plus, they provide info on how to get low-cost internet through government programs and non-profit organizations.

What is it for?
Reaching out to some of them could lead you to getting internet access for your community at affordable prices, with guarantees for maintenance, training, and sustainability that you might not even imagine right now… go for it!

What do you need?

A computer with a web browser and an internet connection.
A web translator like google translate, deepl, or an AI that can help you translate (you can search for “AI for text translation”).
Patience and time to dedicate to the search—it’s better if you do it with others.
A dose of courage to send your request to some of these initiatives… you have all our support! That’s how we did it.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Think of the best question you can ask the internet and dare to dive in to find… you can even do a SOLE!

In the case of Colombia, it could be something like “what initiatives connect rural, remote, and low-income communities to the internet in Colombia?”, or “how to get subsidized internet in Colombia?”, or “what organizations connect communities to low-cost internet in Colombia?” Be creative with your question to find varied answers!
You can also investigate the suggestions in search engines to dive deeper and find more related info.
Don’t be shy about contacting the companies and programs the search engine suggests.


Step 2 → At SOLE Colombia, we know some low-cost connectivity initiatives around the world. Take a look—we encourage you to get in touch with them!


Mintic - “Connecting the Unconnected” program by MINTIC and Colnodo

The “Connecting the Unconnected” program is an initiative by the Ministry of Information and Communications Technologies (MinTIC) of Colombia, which seeks to bring the Internet to rural areas and communities with little or no connectivity.
The Digital Centers are free Wi-Fi access points installed in strategic locations to facilitate internet access in these areas.
Steps to access, according to the program’s website:

Locate a Digital Center: Digital Centers are located in rural areas and communities with little connectivity. You can find information about their location on the MinTIC website.
Turn on your device’s Wi-Fi: Turn on the Wi-Fi on your phone, tablet, or other device you want to connect.
Search for the “MinTIC Conecta” network: Your device will show the available Wi-Fi networks. Select the network named “Mintic Conecta”.
Fill in the requested data: You will be asked to enter some information to register. Complete the required fields.
Accept the terms and conditions: Read the terms and conditions carefully and, if you agree, accept them to connect. You’re all set! Once you’ve completed the steps above, you’ll be able to use the internet connection.


Colnodo

In Colombia, access to the 900 MHz band for communities is being addressed through a public consultation led by the Ministry of Information and Communications Technologies (MinTIC) and the National Spectrum Agency (ANE).
The goal is to make the use of this band more flexible for community networks, especially in rural areas with little or no commercial network coverage.
Process and Participation:

Public Consultation: A public consultation has been opened so that organized communities, community networks, and other interested parties can express their interest and provide comments on the proposal.
Participation Form: An online form is available for communities to describe their situation, interests, and suggestions regarding the use of the band.
Information and Documentation: The ANE has published documents and guidelines for the consultation, which can be viewed and downloaded.
Deadline: The public consultation is open until July 1, 2025.

Focus on Rural Areas:

The 900 MHz band, with its good coverage and penetration capacity, is considered ideal for supporting connectivity in rural and remote areas.
The goal is for community networks to be able to leverage this band to bring connectivity to places where there is no commercial coverage or it is limited.

Potential Benefits:

Community Connectivity: Facilitate internet access for rural communities through community networks.
Economic and Social Development: Boost access to services like telemedicine, virtual education, and other opportunities thanks to connectivity.
Community Empowerment: Community networks can generate experience and autonomy in managing their own networks.
Future Readiness: Experience with this band can pave the way for adopting more advanced technologies and services in the future.

Active Participation:
It is crucial that interested communities participate actively in the public consultation, expressing their needs, expectations, and proposals for the use of the 900 MHz band. Participation from all interested sectors is fundamental to building a strategy that guarantees fair and sustainable connectivity for everyone.
In short, the 900 MHz band represents an opportunity for Colombian communities to access the internet and improve their connectivity, especially in rural areas, through community networks.
The public consultation is the space for communities to express their needs and contribute to building a public policy that recognizes the importance of the spectrum for social and economic development.

Internet Society

Offers funding to organizations that build and expand internet networks in underserved areas, which can result in more affordable options for residents.
Supports the creation of community networks, which are often a more economical alternative to commercial options.

NUPEF

NUPEF.org, through its focus on community networks and affordable internet access, can facilitate access to funding and resources to build or strengthen community internet networks, in addition to offering training to manage and maintain these networks.
It also promotes the creation of safe and inclusive virtual communities, empowering marginalized groups to use technology and advocate for their digital rights:


It can help you apply for grants and funding for community network projects, including building new access solutions or expanding existing ones, especially for marginalized and underserved populations.


Offers training and resources so community members can develop skills in building, managing, and maintaining community networks.


If you already have a network, NUPEF can help strengthen it by improving infrastructure, updating technology, and providing technical support to ensure its continuous operation.


Promotes the creation of safe and welcoming online communities, where diversity is valued and users are protected from violence and abuse.


Works so that excluded people can use and adapt the internet and digital technology for their needs, including developing fair and equitable solutions for universal access.


Seeks economic models that allow for affordable and sustainable internet access, generating value in the community and promoting self-sufficiency.


Facilitates the exchange of knowledge and experiences between different communities and movements, promoting collective action for digital inclusion.


APC


It is a network of civil society organizations that helps people access the internet where there is no connectivity or it is not affordable.
It also supports local and grassroots groups so they can use technology to develop their communities and advance the defense and exercise of their rights.
Promotes government ICT policies that serve the interests of the population, especially in the context of the Global South.

Unconnected

It is an initiative that seeks to connect people who do not have internet access, especially in rural, remote, and low-income areas.
They offer funding programs and resources for communities and local organizations that are working on building and expanding internet infrastructure, such as community networks and complementary access solutions.
Additionally, they provide information on how to get low-cost internet through government programs and non-profit organizations.

High Speed Internet

If you know of any other way to get support to connect your community to the Internet at a low cost, don’t forget to comment on this Solution so we can add it. We also ask that if you see this solution is outdated or has incorrect information, let us know so we can keep researching and taking this information to the ends of the earth.

How do you know if this solution works?
How having low-cost internet can help:

Funding for infrastructure: there are organizations that offer funding to organizations that build and expand internet networks in underserved areas, which can result in more affordable options for residents.
Information on subsidy programs: other organizations provide information on government and non-government programs that offer subsidies or reduced rates for internet access for low-income individuals.
Community networks: others support the creation of community networks, which are often a more economical alternative to commercial options.
Resources to build networks: some others offer a toolkit to build and maintain community networks, which can help reduce infrastructure costs.
Training for the installation and maintenance of equipment and networks.
Strengthening the social fabric and bonds between the community and with the community of practice: initiatives usually include content and practice on digital rights, equity, community ties, and human connection, which make the internet an excuse to have more conscious and connected communities.


Other possible Internets
The continuous search for Internet Solutions has led us at SOLE Colombia to investigate and be curious enough to find the “parceros” (friends/partners) who have helped us bring the internet to very remote places.
In that same way, you—yes, you—having access to this information, can encourage yourself to explore relationships with people and organizations that can guarantee the right that you and your community have to access the internet wherever you are.
When people come together to get things done, the sky’s the limit.

en/solve/solv-find-allied-spaces.title: How to get spaces with the help of partners?
en/solve/solv-find-allied-spaces.summary: Connecting with institutions or organizations that manage spaces.
en/solve/solv-find-allied-spaces.content:
Hi! I’m Catalina. Sometimes it’s easy to find meeting spaces, but other times we need someone to open the door for us. In this solution, we’ve gathered some tips on how to manage spaces through allies.

Remember, managing these spaces is all about weaving trust and building bonds.

What does finding spaces with allies mean?
It’s the process of identifying and talking to organizations that “look after” places (NGOs, foundations, libraries) so they can lend them to you for learning together using the Internet.
It’s about getting someone excited about what you do so they believe in your mission.

Why do it?
A space is an opportunity to turn it into a place for exchange. Weaving bonds will allow you to collaborate in different ways in the future to keep building a more equitable world.

What do you need?

A clear purpose.
Patience (trust is a slow-cooked meal).
Courage to strike up conversations with others.


How to do it?

Tip #1 → Get to know the local players

Look around to see who’s there: local government, NGOs, cooperatives. Ask at the school or town hall which organizations have a presence. Create a directory of potential allies.

Food for thought: Consider what stories have been told in those spaces before and how your proposal adds to what already exists.



Tip #2 → Reach out with purpose

Always try to make contact in person. Tell them about your projects and the importance of having a place to gather the community. If your intention is to host a SOLE, explain how any place can become a learning space.


Tip #3 → Cultivate trust and autonomy

Once you identify an ally, let a bond of trust grow before asking for autonomy to manage the space. Show them that your community is responsible.

Pro-tip: If you need to write a letter, check out How to write an invitation that brings people together?.



How do you know if this solution is working?
When you manage to secure a space thanks to someone else’s support, and when that place starts to be recognized by the community as their own, you’ve hit the mark!

Other possible Internets
Managing shared spaces allows resources that were previously locked away to become common goods. By gathering to learn together, we keep creating other possible internets.

en/solve/solv-find-wifi-app.title: What free networks are available to connect to the internet?
en/solve/solv-find-wifi-app.summary: Scan for nearby WiFi signals using a mobile app.
en/solve/solv-find-wifi-app.content:
Hi there! I’m Belén, and I’m glad you’re here. You might often think you don’t have Internet or that your mobile signal is weak, but if you look closely, there might be a WiFi network nearby with a better connection, or even a free one.

What does it mean to hunt for WiFi signals with an app?
Hunting for WiFi signals with a mobile app means using software on your Smartphone to scan, analyze, and find available wireless networks.

What’s it good for?
Sometimes the spot where we’re standing doesn’t have access, but if we move around a bit, we might just find a network. The WiFi Map app shows us a map with networks within a 2-kilometer radius and even shares the access passwords.
If you want to make the most of a nearby connection, you can use it to run a SOLE (How to run a SOLE?).

What do you need?

Smartphone
Available storage space on your phone.
Mobile data connection (for the initial search).
A spirit of generosity.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Install the app

Open the Google Play Store or App Store and search for WiFi Map. You can also access it through your browser.


Step 2 → Set up the app

Accept the terms of use and grant access to your location. Make sure location services are turned on in your phone’s control panel.



Step 3 → Look for nearby networks

Tap the arrow icon to locate yourself on the map. The closest networks will pop up, along with their passwords.



Step 4 → Select a network

Pick a network to see its details. Sometimes the app will ask you to watch a short video before showing you the password.



How do I know if this solution works?
If you manage to connect to a network and browse at a decent speed to find answers to your Big Questions, then the solution worked!

Other possible Internets
This solution provides temporary access in populated areas where other users have shared their passwords. It’s a form of digital mutual aid.

en/solve/solv-fish-game.title: How to use gaming to learn community equipment care?
en/solve/solv-fish-game.summary: A governance solution for managing common resources.
en/solve/solv-fish-game.content:
▶
Hi there, I’m Mateo. At SOLE, we want more folks to get online and use tech gear together as a group. To take care of these tools that belong to everyone, I’ve got a fun game for you called the Fish Game.

What is the Fish Game?
It’s a hands-on activity to build teamwork skills and get a handle on why cooperating is key for the common good. With this game, the community gets to reflect on how we manage finite resources.

What’s it for?
It’s great for reaching agreements with your community on how to use and look after shared gear (computers, antennas, data plans) without needing any magic formulas—just good old-fashioned conversation.

What do you need?

A bag with at least 80 candies or tokens.
A table and chairs.
Poster board and markers.


How to do it?

Step 1 → First round: Free-for-all
Put 50 tokens (fish) on the table. Each person can “fish” between 0 and 5 tokens per round, without talking. At the end of the round, add 1 fish for every 10 that are left. Watch what happens when everyone just looks out for number one.



Step 2 → Second round: Lean times
The rules are the same, but now explain that there’s a terrible drought. Food is scarce, and they’ve got families to feed. Usually, people fish faster because they’re scared of running out.



Step 3 → Third round: Making deals
Same scarcity situation, but now they get 2 minutes to talk before fishing to decide how to go about it. Watch how the distribution changes when there’s a plan in place.



Step 4 → Reflect on the secret
Tell everyone what the pieces represent: the fishermen are the community, and the fish are the finite resources (equipment, internet, land). The better we look after the resource, the longer it lasts for everyone.



Step 5 → Write down the real agreements
On the poster board, write down the rules for using and taking care of your actual tech gear. Put those commitments in writing so everyone can check them later.



How does the game work?
The game shows us present bias: when we feel like something is going to run out, we consume it irrationally. By reaching agreements, we prevent scarcity and find fair alternatives for everyone.

How much is enough?
This dilemma is known as the Tragedy of the Commons. If everyone only looks out for their own benefit, we destroy the resource that benefits us all. Agreeing is the only way to make technology sustainable.

en/solve/solv-full-server.title: How to build your own Pocket Server (Full Server)?
en/solve/solv-full-server.summary: Extend your local network capabilities with a file manager and PHP app support.
en/solve/solv-full-server.content:
Hi! I’m David. This solution is the natural evolution of the Pocket Internet or giving a second life to an old computer. Here, we’re going to transform that machine into a robust server capable of managing files and more complex applications.

What’s it for?
By setting up a “Full” server, you give your community a digital meeting point where they can easily upload and download files, like a local cloud, but without needing the internet. It’s a toolkit that can be passed from hand to hand via a USB connection.

An analogy to understand it (Possibility)
If it helps you visualize it, you can think of this server as a Community Kitchen:

The RAM Memory is the prep table where you get the information ready.
The Storage is the pantry where you keep the ingredients (files) for good.
This server is the space where everyone can come to look for “recipes” (information) or drop off their own ingredients.


What do you need?

A computer with Linux or a Raspberry Pi.
Internet connection (only for the initial setup).
A USB Flash Drive.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Connect via Terminal

Access your machine through a Terminal using SSH.



Step 2 → Create the public directory

We’re going to define the folder where all the shared information will live:
mkdir www
chmod 777 www



Step 3 → Install application support

We’ll install the necessary packages so the server can run dynamic web applications (PHP):
sudo apt install php-fpm php-mbstring php-mysql php-curl php-gd php-zip php-xml -y



Step 4 → Configure the web server

You need to tweak the Nginx configuration so it recognizes the new folder and the PHP language. This is done in the /etc/nginx/sites-available/default file.



Step 5 → Install the File Manager

So anyone can upload files from their browser without using code, we’ll install Tiny File Manager:
cd www
wget raw.githubusercontent.com/prasathmani/tinyfilemanager.php



How to know if it works?
Visit solevoltaje.local/tinyfilemanager.php. If you can see the file manager, your server is ready for action!

en/solve/solv-funding-community-internet.title: How to crowdfund community resources?
en/solve/solv-funding-community-internet.summary: Organize a collection to keep the community internet running.
en/solve/solv-funding-community-internet.content:
Hi, I’m Sanjay, and one of my big passions is putting the resources we have to community use. I like tinkering, sure, but I’m also interested in how we humans coordinate to live better together.
What does it mean to run a collection for community internet?
This solution gathers ideas on how to raise money to pay for a community connection—in other words, getting a community to agree on financially supporting a resource that will be used and enjoyed by everyone.

What’s it for?
Finding ways to organize ourselves to acquire things that improve our living conditions is sometimes a complex task.
If you’re clear that you need the Internet, but don’t know how to get your community on board, get them to back the maintenance and sustainability of the contract, or you don’t know the steps to take to do it together, you can find some useful guidance in this solution.

What do you need?

A very clear idea of why you want to raise the money.
Charisma, a way with words, and people skills to convince folks to join the collection.
Organization to keep the books, manage the money, and keep your contributors updated on how the collection is going and the status of the accounts.
Communication skills to keep collaborators informed about the service status, maintenance needs, or any issues. Also, to receive suggestions or handle the paperwork required for formalizing or maintaining the service.


How to do it?
These recommendations are relevant when running money collections for community purposes. They don’t necessarily have to be followed in order, nor are they the only ones, but we believe they can help you.

Step 1 → Moment 1: Let’s build a team; it’s easier with others

Look for partners to start this campaign.
When we undertake projects for the common good, it’s easy to find allies to share responsibilities. When you do these kinds of initiatives alone, you can quickly get tired and give up, but with others, this project will be much more manageable.
Define who will handle what; that will make the work more organized and allow you to follow up more easily.


Step 2 → Let’s give the collection a purpose, something clear that gets us excited

It’s important to take the time to reflect and think about what we want to do. What is it that we want to achieve? Remember, money is just a means to reach something bigger and more important… that’s called purpose.
In this case, what is it that unites us in this collection, that inspires us to move to get the funds? When you are establishing the purpose of any project, it’s time to tirelessly ask ourselves why, until we are convinced.
Doing SOLE is a great way to find a purpose for the collection. Besides paying for it together, you can learn, talk, and create flourishing communities by using the internet as a group. Paying for the internet together allows you to use it for SOLE, or for anything else you can think of!
For example:

Why do we want internet in a public access space? So that people in my community can learn new things they need or want to learn, converse and dialogue with other people and communities in a Great Conversation, and take action in a self-organized way to live better together.
Why do we want people in our community to be able to learn together? So that it’s not necessary to depend exclusively on learning spaces and people related to the educational system, to realize that anyone can learn anything using the internet. Why in a group? Because going anywhere alone is a difficult path; instead, when we do it together, it’s better.
Why do we want them to be able to converse through the internet? Interacting with other people with the goal of learning or letting others be part of our lives always makes us feel better. Learning together when there are other people who participate in our findings and with whom we can walk the path together makes us feel that what we learn transcends and is bigger than us. If we connect with each other through the internet, it’s because we are mutually interested and can accompany each other; we are not alone on the path… Do you want to connect with people around the world in your SOLE sessions? Take a look at La Nube de Abuelitas SOLE! They are volunteers from all over the world who connect to SOLE sessions to accompany, offer warm encouragement, share, learn, and have fun together.
Why do we want to help our community flourish? So that we all have a happier, fuller, and more enjoyable life!

Does it make sense to have public access internet in our community? Absolutely!


Step 3 → Let’s identify potential people interested in participating

Which of our neighbors would be interested in having community internet? What interest might they have in contributing money to this project? This way, we can translate our project into their potential interests.
Here are some examples of SOLEros who have self-organized to learn together using the internet:

Elainer, when she used SOLE so that the young people in her community could learn to make video games.
Robinson, who used SOLE so that his community could find sustainable alternatives to their traditional crops.
María, when, through SOLE, she got her students to take responsibility for their own educational process and changed the way they research and learn at their school.




Step 4 → A story, the best way to communicate an idea

Now that we know who we are going to direct our campaign to, let’s create a story. We recommend answering five fundamental questions: who, what, when, where, and why.
Here is ours:
In the community of La Piche, delicious honey is produced. Everyone in the community works in trades related to the production of this delicious honey: some have hives, others collect the honey, others sell it, some make related products…
We are a group of young people interested in creating natural cosmetic products based on honey and beeswax, but we don’t know how to start making those products, nor the tools we need, nor the permits we require, or how we could market them, etc. We want to start with: how can we make a honey and beeswax lip balm?
Using the Internet, we could find answers to these and other Great Questions!
The cheapest Internet plan is 120,000 COP, and no one in the village could pay for it. But we have thought that by collecting money among 12 people or families, we could pay a monthly fee of 10,000 COP and put the fiber optic broadband internet in a place with easy access for everyone, such as the nursing home, the community hall, or Doña Adela’s shop, which is the business that is open most of the time and where we could all connect. We could all use the connection, even the children in the village, to do their homework.
So, if you are interested and can be part of this collection, join this list! Soon we will be able to have internet for ourselves!
I will send all expenses and receipt payments on the first of each month to a WhatsApp group, and we can keep up with any news there.
Are you in?


Step 5 → Buy, communicate, and organize expenses

With the money collected, you just have to make the purchase.
Remember that none of these contracts have long-term lock-in clauses, so if you are not satisfied with the service, you can cancel it and switch to another operator.
It is important to be organized with the accounts and communicate payments and any news or issues immediately to everyone involved.
This way, everyone can be co-responsible for any decision regarding this collection and can assume the responsibilities or consequences together.
Make sure to create a communication flow with your collaborators so you can communicate in both directions and quickly solve any problems that may arise.

How do you know if this solution works?
With this solution, you manage to organize neighbors toward a common good, embodied in the payment of a service, to take advantage of it collectively and get the most out of it.
You also manage to improve the connectivity conditions of the place where we live, making it a place where life is better.

Other possible Internets
Organizing ourselves to get things done will take us as far as we want to go.
In this case, it allows us to have a shared internet public access point. It is important to measure the bandwidth offered by the service to be contracted very well. This way, we will be able to contract a service that is fast and powerful enough in relation to the number of people we want to link to that connection.
The next step would be how to improve the conditions of this connectivity without a significant increase in costs.

en/solve/solv-improve-signal-can.title: How to boost my mobile signal with a soda can?
en/solve/solv-improve-signal-can.summary: Build a little antenna for your phone.
en/solve/solv-improve-signal-can.content:
Hi! It’s a pleasure to meet you. My name is Mateo, and I’ll be your guide through this project. If you’re reading, listening, or watching this, it’s because you’re interested or curious about how to boost your cell phone signal in a very simple way. If that’s the case, you’re in the right place.

What is this solution for?
This solution helps improve your cell phone signal temporarily. In other words, it gives it a boost, but keep in mind that signal quality also depends on external factors like the weather, your surroundings, your carrier, and the number of towers emitting radio waves around you to allow for calls or internet browsing.
The solution I’m sharing with you is a simple, quick, and very interesting option. You’ll see that the results of this test are exciting and eye-opening.

What do you need?


One person is enough to work on this solution. Although, everything is easier when you have company. Give it a go!
A clean metal can (a soda or beverage can works).
Scissors.
A utility knife (optional).
A ruler, preferably metal.
A fine-point marker.
Thick clear tape.
Safety gloves.


Before we start, a few safety tips
Even though this solution has a basic difficulty level, it’s important to keep a few safety recommendations in mind:

Work on a flat, rigid surface, preferably a table where you can cut safely.
Find a clean can that isn’t rusty.
We recommend being in a quiet place without distractions, and having plenty of time and patience.
Keep your hands at a safe distance from the cuts you’ll be making with the scissors or utility knife.
Preferably, wear safety gloves.
We recommend sitting in a comfortable place to work.


How to do it?
This solution has 3 steps that I’ll walk you through. Keep in mind that some parts might be frustrating and others very exciting, and both are perfectly fine; that’s all part of the “tinkering” process. The important thing is to keep trying. Let’s get started!

Step 1 → Draw the base metal sheet

To begin, get all the materials mentioned ready.
Next, cut the base and the top of the can with the scissors or utility knife so that you have an open sheet; imagine it’s a rectangular piece of paper. You can do this using scissors or a utility knife. Place the beverage can on a flat, rigid surface, preferably a table.

⚠️⚠️ Do this patiently and carefully, keeping your hand at a safe distance from the cut you are making. Remember that the can edges are sharp.


Once you have the rectangular sheet cut out, flatten it until you’ve removed as many irregularities as possible from the surface. Imagine it should look like a smooth sheet of paper. This will be the metal sheet we’ll work with from here on out.
Using the ruler and the fine-point marker, draw a 4cm x 4cm square on the metal sheet.

⚠️⚠️ Be careful when making all cuts. If you have them, I recommend using safety gloves.




Step 2 → Turn the can into an antenna

Cut out the 4 cm x 4 cm square you drew using the scissors until you have a square metal sheet.

Now, choose one of the edges of this square sheet and mark the center with a fine-point marker—that is, 2 centimeters from the edge.
Place the ruler on the center point you marked, and with the marker, make two marks 0.5 cm on each side of the center. Repeat this same step on the opposite edge of the side you are working on. Connect the marks and draw the lines so you have a 1 cm rectangle.

  
    
      
    
    
      
    
  


💬❓ How are you doing so far? If your can looks like the last image 👆🏽, we’re on the right track. If not, you can try again by following the same steps. No rush, I’ll be here waiting!

Continue drawing marks every 0.5 cm on each of the two lines you already drew. By the end, you should have 7 marks on each of the lines as seen in this image:

Draw lines from side to side for each of the marks you made in the previous step. Then, cut along the 7 lines you made, without cutting the central column that is 1cm wide.

If your can looks like this 👆🏽, you can proceed to fold one tab, skip one: fold the second, the fourth, the sixth, and the eighth. Then, you must trim each of the tabs that were folded.
Finally, cover your metal piece on both sides with thick clear tape; this will help protect it so it lasts longer.

  
    
      
    
    
      
    
  

We’re done! Now, the easy part: using your can to improve your mobile signal.

Step 3 → Install your antenna on your cell phone
The main antenna of most cell phones is usually located on the back, in the upper right corner.
Use clear tape to stick this metal piece in the mentioned spot and protect it, preferably with the phone case you are using.

🎉💪🏽 We’re done! Now you’re ready to enjoy a better signal. Congratulations on finishing this solution; I hope this journey was challenging and exciting.
Like this one, you can find many more solutions at Voltaje to connect without fear of using the internet as a group. Go ahead and keep browsing! See more solutions →

How do you know if this solution works?

The easiest way is to check if the signal bars or dots on your phone (located in the top left or right corner of your screen) change with and without the can. These bars measure how strong the signal you’re receiving is. In theory, the more bars you have, the better the signal you should be receiving.
Another option is to measure the download speed on your phone. Check out the solution How to test your Internet connection speed? →.
This solution can achieve a significant improvement in your cell phone’s signal reception by one or at most two bars or dots. Keep in mind that the signal cannot improve in places where there has never been a signal.


Other possible Internets
Keep in mind that there are two types of signals: your cell phone signal, which you use to make calls and send text messages, and the WiFi signal, which you use to connect to the internet.
With this solution, you can improve both signals because it amplifies the reception and transmission of waves from the antenna built into your phone. It’s a little “boost” for that antenna. You can test this solution in different conditions and draw your own conclusions about whether it’s working for you or not.
But also, boosting your cell phone signal can help you share the internet with other people who need it. Group internet is safer and can help others with their work, studies, or enjoying various entertainment activities.
We invite you to be part of a new way of using the internet together! 💪🏽 Boost your signal, enjoy it, and share your internet.
Thanks for making it to the end of this solution. We hope it was useful! And if it was, share it with other people who you know could use it.
See you soon! 👋🏽

en/solve/solv-improve-signal-router.title: How to boost your modem signal?
en/solve/solv-improve-signal-router.summary: Some tips to get the most out of your router.
en/solve/solv-improve-signal-router.content:
Hi! I’m Manu, the storyteller for SOLE Colombia, and I’ve also felt that frustration of losing my Internet connection right in the middle of an important meeting or a SOLE session.
What does improving your router signal mean?
Just when you need it most, the connection disappears—has that happened to you? It has to me, more than once. But don’t worry, because you’re about to learn how to improve the signal of your Router so that happens less often.
I’ll also show you how to tweak your Router settings to browse faster by changing the servers for DNS and adjusting your WiFi channel. This isn’t hard, and you can do it right from home! So get ready, we’re going to get the most out of your network.

What is this for?
I’m going to walk you through getting the most out of your Router. Together, we’ll improve how the WiFi signal is distributed in your space, achieving a more stable connection so it doesn’t fail you when you need it most—whether it’s for a meeting, a class, or a SOLE session. No more interrupted signals when you’re investigating a Big Question!
Remember, these tweaks won’t increase the speed you’re paying for, but they will help the signal reach every corner of your house better by optimizing your DNS.

What do you need?

To use an Internet service that connects through a Router.
The login credentials for your Router.
A computer connected to the network.
A bit of patience (hopefully not too much!).
A tinkerer’s attitude.


How to do it?
Alright, I’m going to guide you step-by-step to improve your WiFi signal. Trust me! Something is bound to change!

Step 1 → Measure your connection speed

The first thing you need to do is measure your current connection speed. In this solution, we tell you how to do it: ¿Cómo saber la velocidad de tu conexión a Internet?
Knowing your speed will let you compare the “before” and “after” once you’ve made the adjustments.


Step 2 → Explore your space and locate the Router

It might seem obvious, but we often forget the simplest thing: get closer to the Router. If you’re organizing a SOLE session or have several devices connected, make sure they are as close as possible so the signal hits harder.
Where you put the Router is key. Make sure to place it in an elevated spot, like on a table or even mounted on the wall. Ideally, it should be in a central location, not in a corner or near a window, which is where installers often leave them. Moving the Router to a more strategic spot will help the signal spread more evenly throughout the house.

Photo taken from Pexels, (2024).

Photo taken by Manuela Córdoba, (2024).

Step 3 → Position the Router antennas perpendicularly

Have you looked at your router’s antennas? Check them right now. An important detail to improve the signal is to make sure they are in a perpendicular position—that is, pointing toward the ceiling. This helps the signal waves distribute better.


Make that adjustment and you’ll notice the difference. Well done!
With these 3 actions, you should already see some improvement. If you want to go further, check out the more advanced steps below.


Step 4 → Configure the DNS

What the heck is that?
DNS is like an address book that helps your computer find websites faster. By using faster DNS servers, like Google’s or Cloudflare’s, you ensure that pages load with more speed. The default servers from your Internet provider aren’t always the most optimal, so switching to more efficient ones can improve your browsing experience.
Now we’re going to do something interesting: configure the DNS. This will help the web pages you visit load faster, since DNS are the directories of IP addresses that the Router consults when browsing.
If you want to switch to faster and more reliable DNS servers, it will make your Internet queries snappier. To do this, follow these steps:

Access your Router’s admin interface. To do this, in your computer’s network settings, look for the gateway. There you will find an IP address, something like 192.168.0.1 or 192.168.1.1.
Log in with the credentials, which are usually admin/admin, or check your device’s manual for the default passwords.
Change the values to 1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1 (from Cloudflare) and 8.8.8.8 (from Google).
Open your browser and enter that address in the address bar. This will take you to the Router control panel.
Look for the Network Settings section, and there, the DNS Servers option.
Save the changes and restart the Router.

Very good! Now your network will use these DNS servers, which are faster and more reliable.


Step 5 → Configure the WiFi channel

Another key adjustment is the WiFi channel configuration. Channels determine the frequency at which the Router broadcasts the signal. To avoid interference with other nearby networks, set your Router to the recommended channels: 1, 6, or 11. To do this:

Enter your Router’s configuration interface again.
Look for the Wireless section.
Choose one of the recommended channels: 1, 6, or 11.
Save the changes and restart the Router.

With this adjustment, you’ll reduce interference and improve signal quality. Great job, we’re almost done!

How do I know if this solution works?
Did you manage it? I’m sure you did! By following these steps, I’m sure your Router signal will have improved, and therefore, the distribution of WiFi in your space.

Other possible Internets
Although you won’t be able to increase the speed beyond what you’re paying for :c, you will have ensured that every corner of your house receives a stronger and more stable signal.
I hope these tips are useful to you and that you no longer have Internet cutouts in the middle of an important meeting or an exciting investigation in SOLE.

en/solve/solv-install-3G-antenna.title: How to install my 3G/4G antenna?
en/solve/solv-install-3G-antenna.summary: Installing an antenna to get Internet in a fixed spot.
en/solve/solv-install-3G-antenna.content:
Hi, I’m Sanjay. While I’m no connectivity expert, I’ve learned by tinkering: that is, through trial and error and asking others about it. Today, I’ll walk you through installing your own antenna!
It’s important to know that there are many types of 3G or 4G antennas, though, in general, this guide should help you install whichever one you have. Your antenna might come with a manual or instructions. We recommend reading that first.

What is installing a 3G/4G antenna?
In short, it’s setting up and getting a device running that helps improve cellular signal access in an area where it was previously weak. Keep in mind that for this solution, you need to have the antenna on hand. If you don’t have one yet, you can head over to the solution How to buy a 3G-4G antenna? to figure out which one works best for you.

What is it for?
There are places where cellular phone signal is very weak. An antenna can help you get better connection quality.
What the antenna does is capture and amplify the specific cellular data signal (3G or 4G). Once it’s at your height, the signal can be shared over the air using a WiFi network, or by cable using a modem or router.

Before you start…

Attention: Remember that you are working with electrical equipment. Be careful when plugging things into the power outlet. Be mindful of weather conditions, especially the risk of storms.


What do you need?


The 3G-4G antenna you purchased.
Coaxial cable to bring in the signal.
Modem or Router with its accessories.
SIM card from the operator with the best signal.
Computer with Ethernet connection or Smartphone.
A tall, sturdy pole.
Supports and tools to secure the pole.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Define the installation spot

Before unpacking, define where you want the modem and the antenna to be permanently located. The modem needs electricity, so identify the power outlet.



Step 2 → Identify the cell towers

For antennas to work best, they should point toward the nearest tower. Identify the closest cell tower, usually found on mountain peaks.



Step 3 → Insert the SIM and connect the modem

Insert the SIM card into the modem tray. Make sure the contacts line up.


Tip: Make sure the SIM size is the right one for your modem.

Connect the power cable and turn the device on. Check the indicator lights.


Step 4 → Connect and hoist the antenna

Attach the antenna to the highest end of the pole. Unroll the coaxial cable and connect it to the antenna and the modem.



Step 5 → Connect your devices

Turn on the WiFi on your computer or Smartphone and search for the modem’s network. The password is usually on a label on the device.

You’re doing great: If you’ve managed to connect, congratulations! You’re ready to browse.




Step 6 → Secure the antenna permanently

Once you find the best direction for the signal, anchor the pole to the wall or support securely.



How to know if this solution works?
If you see the signal indicators in green on your modem and you can open web pages on your devices, your installation has been a success!

Other possible Internets
This solution is ideal for community spaces like schools or libraries. It allows many people to connect at the same time. If there is no mobile signal at all, you can explore the The Disconnected section.

en/solve/solv-internet-quality-diagnosis.title: How to check your mobile signal strength without a speed test?
en/solve/solv-internet-quality-diagnosis.summary: Signal types and how to figure out if your connection is actually decent.
en/solve/solv-internet-quality-diagnosis.content:
Hi, I’m Manuela. I’m the storyteller for SOLE Colombia, and even though I don’t know much about tech, I’ve started to get a kick out of tinkering and learning things that keep getting me out of jams.
What does it mean to know how good your signal is?
An Internet connection isn’t a ghost that follows us everywhere… or maybe it is a little bit of a ghost!
This is a way for you to learn a bit more about what the Internet is, how to figure out what’s failing at any given moment, or how to improve your signal.

What is it for?
Knowing how good your Internet connection is can give you clues to understand its performance and troubleshoot potential issues.
For example, it will let you know if the speed you signed up for with your mobile or internet provider is actually what you’re getting… or if they’re pulling a fast one on you.
You can identify the spots in your community, or your house, where you have the best signal. That way, you’ll know where that movie you’re watching might hang, or where you should stand to get a better call.
You’ll be able to make decisions if you need to restart the router, or change the reception channel of your WiFi signal. Or even determine if your modem needs replacing.
By optimizing your signal, you’ll have a faster and more stable connection to do SOLE or access certain content that requires a better signal.

What do you need?

Your device (cell phone or tablet)
To be connected to an Internet signal


How to do it?

Step 1 → Grab your phone and check if you have mobile signal

Look at one of the top corners of your phone. You’ll find some mobile signal bars there: If you see one or more bars, it means the phone is receiving a signal and reading your SIM card.

Step 2 → How strong is your connection?

Strength isn’t the same as speed. The little bars measure the RSSI (Received Signal Strength Indicator), which is the power. Think of this like the volume of a voice in a room: when there are more bars, it means someone is speaking loudly; when there are few bars, it means someone is whispering.
However, just because you hear someone loudly doesn’t guarantee they’re speaking fast. Your actual internet speed depends on the bandwidth available at the tower and how many people are connected at the same time.
The more bars you have, the more power the mobile signal you’re receiving has. You need both, power and speed, to do different things on the Internet. If you don’t have a way to measure your connection speed, you can get an idea of the speed based on the type of connection.


Step 3 → What type of mobile connection do you have and what are they for?

Look next to the mobile signal bars and you’ll see some letters indicating the type of signal you have. These letters refer to the speeds and technologies that operators use to send you information (Internet data).
Found them? If so, check the list below to see what you can do with each one.

G: This is the abbreviation for the GPRS signal type, the slowest of all technologies. It’s a second-generation or 2G network that only allows you to send text messages.
E: This is the abbreviation for the EDGE signal type, it’s an improved version of GPRS, also called 2.5G, and it’s useful for simple internet searches.


3G: Also called UMTS, it’s a third-generation network, designed for browsing multimedia content.
H: Uses HSPA technology; it’s something like an improved 3G. It’s more than enough to access social networks or listen to music on the Internet.
H+: It’s an evolved HSPA for watching videos online or downloading them faster.
4G: This is the technology also called LTE, considered the fourth generation or 4G. The speed of this network reaches 100 Mbps download and 50 Mbps upload, this is what we call “broadband.” Super fast!
5G: It’s the fastest technology of all, for now, and can be 100 times faster than 4G. You need a phone that supports 5G to be able to use it.




Step 4 → How good is your connection?

How many bars do you see? What type of signal do you have? Now that you’ve explored these questions, you can have an idea of how good your connection is without running a speed test. Remember, with the different types of signal you can…

G: only send text messages
E: browse web pages
3G, H, H+: browse social networks, listen to music, and watch videos
4G, LTE: have video calls and watch high-definition videos




How to know if this solution works?
If you managed to identify how many signal bars you have and the type of signal, you’ll be able to know how good your connection is, and if you know that, you’ve achieved the goal of this solution!

Other possible Internets
Internet speed tests need… Internet. So, in situations where the connection is very low or slow, speed meters might not even work. In those cases, this solution is super useful!
It also helps you better understand what the different codes on your phone mean and even get to know the current connectivity situation of the place where you are. If the signal is really bad, you can rally your neighbors to look for spots with better connection together, or even chip in for a shared Internet plan or some other connectivity solution to use the Internet as a group.

en/solve/solv-internet-speedtest.title: How to check your internet connection speed?
en/solve/solv-internet-speedtest.summary: Run a speed test on your internet connection.
en/solve/solv-internet-speedtest.content:
Hi, I’m Belén. Until very recently, I didn’t know you could test the speed of your internet connection. I found it really easy and super useful to learn how to do it because it lets me know the status of my connection at any given moment.
Understanding why some things aren’t working for me at certain times gives me peace of mind and helps me look for solutions. Would you like to learn how to do it too? Let’s get started! 🧭💪🏽

What is an internet speed test?
An internet speed test is a tool that measures how fast your connection is by evaluating your download and upload speeds, as well as your latencia de red.

What is it for?
A speed test is useful for a few things.


It’s handy for verifying if the speed you’re paying your provider for matches the actual speed you’re getting. This lets you make informed decisions about your internet service provider. For example: Am I actually getting what they promised? Is it worth sticking with this provider? Are there others that offer a better connection?


It also helps you identify connection problems, or spots and situations where your signal is better or worse. For example, to 4G, you need to measure the speed several times until you find the direction where you get the best reception.


Knowing the quality of your internet also lets you know which services you can access. For example, do you know what speed you need to watch a video on YouTube? Keep reading to find out!👇🏽



What do you need?

The device you’re going to connect to the internet with (cell phone, computer, tablet, etc.)
Access to a website or a measurement app, like “Fast”, “Speedtest”, or nPerf. There are also mobile apps like Speedtest by Ookla.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Access a speed test service

You can run your test right here 👇🏽

  
  
  
    This measurement is possible thanks to Meter.net
  

If that doesn’t work for you, here are a few more options:

Web services: Fast →, Speedtest → or nPerf →.
There are also mobile apps like Speedtest by Ookla →.



Step 2 → Run the test

Start the test on the website or app. Wait a few seconds until the number stabilizes.
If you need to take a new measurement, press the restart button.

Heads up: Remember that every time you run a test, you’re using data. So, if you have a limited data plan, try to run tests only when necessary.



Step 3 → Interpret the results

The results generally show your download speed, upload speed, and latencia. Let me break it down for you:

Download speed: This is the speed at which you can receive data from the internet, like when downloading files or watching videos. The higher, the better.
Upload speed: This is the speed at which you can send data to the internet, like when sending emails or uploading videos to social media. Here too, the higher, the better.
Latency (ping): This is the time it takes for a signal to travel back and forth between your device and a remote servidor, measured in milliseconds.
Here, a lower ping is better, especially for online gaming, video calls, or high-quality videos.


💬❓ Now for the big question, how much speed is enough? Go to este enlace to find out how much speed you need to access different services.

Now that you know your internet speed and the speed you need to access different services, you can see more solutions → that will allow you to get, improve, or share your internet.


Additional considerations:

Conexión por cable vs. WiFi: Speed tests via cable (Ethernet) are usually more accurate than WiFi tests, as WiFi connections can be affected by interference.
Servidores de prueba: Some services let you choose the test server to get more accurate results or to test different locations.
Interpreting the results: Compare the results with the speed you’re paying your provider for and consider factors like the time of day and the activity on your red, as this can affect the results.


How do you know if this solution works?
If you managed to get the upload and download values and the latency of your internet connection, you’ve accomplished the first part of the solution. Congratulations!
Beyond the technical side, this solution works when it allows people like you to:

Verify internet connection performance, so you have more information to make decisions, for example, regarding your internet provider.
Diagnose connection problems to, for example, identify places where there is better or worse connection.
Optimize your online experience, so you can adjust your activities to what you need. For example, you can avoid downloading heavy files during peak hours, close windows you aren’t using, or disconnect devices to avoid overloading the modem, among other things.


Other possible Internets
Diagnosing the state of connectivity in remote contexts is fundamental to knowing which type of connectivity solution is most appropriate for each context.

For us at SOLE, it has been very important to know how to do this when we go to work with communities. We’ve discovered that having a complete experience of the internet, where people learn to recognize their own connection conditions, as well as the fluctuations and inconveniences typical of the place where a solution is going to be installed, encourages people to get more hooked. It’s a very powerful and intense strategy to promote self-organized learning.
Feeling capable of establishing or improving the internet signal so it can be used as a group makes everything more powerful… you can see the stories in the sección de inspiraciones → of Voltaje⚡⚡.

en/solve/solv-jangala-install-box.content:
Hi! My name is Catalina. I recently came across the Jangala Big Box, and I think it’s a brilliant connectivity solution! This is the first solution I’m writing to share on Voltaje. It’ll be short and sweet; I hope you find it useful. Let’s get to it!

What is installing a Jangala Big Box?
A Jangala Big Box is a very powerful modem that can capture different types of signals and redistribute them to up to 100 people.
In this solution, I’ll walk you through accessing the Big Box installation manual, where you’ll find instructions on how to link different signal sources (SIM card, wired antennas, among others) to the device.

What is it for?
To install the Jangala Big Box yourself and enjoy the internet as a community.

Heads up: Keep in mind that you need to have a Jangala for this solution to be useful. Check out the solution El internet en una caja: Big Box de Jangala to find out how to get a Jangala Big Box.


What do you need?

A Jangala Big Box.
A device to connect to the internet (smartphone, tablet, computer, or any other).
Internet connection.
A bit of focus.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Go to the Jangala website

Go to the instructions section of the Jangala website by clicking this link →.
Once you’re there, you’ll see several blue buttons. Choose the one in your preferred language. A new window will open, and you’ll be able to see the instructions.


Step 2 → Download the instructions

It’s possible that the place where you’re checking this information (good connectivity) isn’t the same place where you’re going to install your Jangala (low connectivity).
If that’s your case, you can download the instructions to your smartphone or computer so you always have them handy.

en/solve/solv-jangala-internet-box.title: Internet in a box: Jangala's Big Box
en/solve/solv-jangala-internet-box.summary: Manage and configure a powerful wireless internet router.
en/solve/solv-jangala-internet-box.content:
Hi, I’m Sanjay. While I’m no connectivity expert, I’ve learned by tinkering—you know, trial and error, digging around online with others, and learning from folks who’ve been there, done that. Let me give you the lowdown on Jangala’s Big Box 👇🏽
▶
Video conceived, created, and produced by SOLE Colombia, 2024

What does managing a Jangala Big Box look like?
With this solution, you can reach out to an organization in England that offers a powerful portable modem called the Big Box, which lets up to 100 people connect to the internet at the same time.
The organization behind it is called Jangala, and they’re dedicated to providing internet access to people who need urgent humanitarian aid.

Heads up: It’s important to know these devices aren’t for personal use, and you’ll need to meet some eligibility criteria. They’re the ones who evaluate whether your community or project is a good fit for their product.


What’s it for?
Imagine a community with zero connectivity. Now, picture everyone suddenly getting online through a single WiFi network. What would happen?
For starters, an entire community could chip in for one internet plan and share the connection. Even better, they could do it using everyday devices like computers or tablets.
The Jangala Big Box is a lightweight device that turns any internet source into an easy-to-manage WiFi network, supporting anywhere from dozens to thousands of users.

What do you need?

An internet connection and a computer.
To understand English or be ready to use DeepL.
Confidence in your ability to manage the project.
To be in a situation of digital exclusion to qualify as a recipient.


How do you do it?

Step 1 → Find the application form

Head over to Jangala get box and look for the “Request a Box” section. There, you can decide if you need the smaller Get Box or the Big Box.



Step 2 → Fill out the online form

You’ll need to answer the questions in the form. This helps Jangala configure a Big Box that best fits your community’s needs.
The questionnaire covers sections about you, your location, your WiFi setup, and the expected impact.


Step 3 → Wait for a reply and start the conversation

It might take a few weeks to hear back from the Jangala team. They’ll write to the email address you provided in the form.

Keep your chin up: Be patient and keep an eye on your inbox… that moment you get the reply is going to be super exciting!



Step 4 → Plan and receive the equipment

Once you’ve sorted out how Jangala will ship the gear, it shouldn’t take more than a couple of weeks to arrive.

Heads up: It’s super important to make it clear that this is goods with no commercial value to help it clear customs smoothly.



Step 5 → Install the Big Box

Finally, all that’s left is to install the Big Box where you’ll be using it, and you’re good to go!

How do you know if this solution is right for you?
You’ll know the day you get a response from Jangala. If you’re a charity or a group with a shared purpose, Jangala will love to get to know you.
Remember that the Boxes provide WiFi using any kind of internet signal (3G/4G, landline, satellite) and can even use an external antenna.

Other possible Internets
The Jangala Big Box is a great chance to get free or very low-cost connectivity for your whole community. Just imagine the learning possibilities if you all use the internet together!

en/solve/solv-know-ram.title: How to check how much RAM I have?
en/solve/solv-know-ram.summary: Learn how to check your computer's memory to see if it's ready for new tasks.
en/solve/solv-know-ram.content:
Hi! I’m David. I’ve managed to figure out how my gear works through trial and error, and today I want to share a quick way to peek under the hood of your computer.

What is RAM?
RAM memory is like a workbench in a kitchen. It’s fast for keeping ingredients handy, but as soon as you turn off the computer, it gets wiped clean. If the workbench is too small, everything slows down.

What’s it for?
Knowing how much RAM you have helps you understand if your computer can handle running many programs at once or if it’s going to “freeze up” with heavy tasks like video editing.

What do you need?

Your computer (Windows or Mac) turned on.
A couple of minutes.


How to do it
On Windows (10 and 11)

Step 1 → Check the settings

Press the Windows key + i. Go to “System” and look for “About”. Find where it says “Installed RAM”.


Step 2 → Use the Task Manager

Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc. Click on Performance and then on Memory. You’ll see how much you’re using right now.

You’re on the right track: If the graph is very high, your workbench is full.


On Mac computers

Step 3 → Use the Apple menu

Click on the Apple icon () and select “About This Mac”. You’ll clearly see the word Memory.


Step 4 → Use the Terminal

Open the Terminal and type: vm_stat. This will show you technical information about memory usage.


Recommendations

If you have 4GB of RAM, try not to have too many tabs open.
With 8GB, you can work comfortably on most tasks.
If you notice constant sluggishness, it might be time to think about a second life for your equipment.


How do you know if this solution works?
If you managed to see the number (e.g., 8 GB) and understand if you’re using a lot or a little, congratulations! You know your tool a bit better now.

en/solve/solv-know-wifi-passwords.title: How to see saved WiFi passwords on my phone?
en/solve/solv-know-wifi-passwords.summary: Find (and share) the passwords stored on your phone.
en/solve/solv-know-wifi-passwords.content:
Hi, I’m Belén. If there’s one thing I appreciate about this new era of smartphones, it’s the time saved by not having to type in the WiFi password every single time you connect. But where are they stored? And how can you share them?

What does knowing your phone’s WiFi passwords mean?
With this solution, you’ll be able to dig up the WiFi passwords already stored on your phone. If you want to do a SOLE session in a place you’ve been before, you can get reconnected without any hassle.

What’s it for?
It’s for making internet access easier for your community. If you already have the password, you can share it with other devices so everyone can start their research and solve Big Questions (How to do a SOLE?).

What do you need?

A phone with an Android Operating System.
At least one saved password.
Curiosity.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Explore your passwords

Go to your phone’s “Settings” and then to the WiFi section. Tap on the network you’re already connected to. A QR code with the info will pop up. Take a screenshot of this image.



Step 2 → Decode the password

Since you can’t use your own phone’s scanner on its own screenshot, head over to the Zxing website in your browser. Upload the image and hit “Submit Query.” The network name and the password will appear.



Step 3 → Share with your community

You’re all set! Now you can share these details with whoever needs them. That way, all the groups can get connected and start tinkering together.


How to know if this solution works?
If your teammates manage to connect to the network using the details you found, you nailed it! You’ve made community connection that much easier.

en/solve/solv-need-3Gantenna.title: Do I need a 3G/4G antenna?
en/solve/solv-need-3Gantenna.summary: Find the antenna that fits your setup.
en/solve/solv-need-3Gantenna.content:
Hi, I’m Sanjay. Along with Gabriel, another fellow tinkerer, we made our first purchase of a 4G antenna after digging into commercial solutions for connectivity issues.
In this guide, I’m going to share some tips to help you buy a 4G antenna.

What is a 3G or 4G antenna?
3G and 4G are just shorthand for the set of technologies used to transmit voice and data over mobile networks.
To get online, your devices need to be smartphones.

What is a 3G/4G antenna for?
Internet signals travel through invisible electromagnetic waves. Smartphones have a small antenna inside them that catches these waves.
Buying a commercial antenna is one of the best ways to get a stable connection in a fixed spot, like a school or a library. What the antenna does is catch and amplify the signal, bringing it down through a cable to where you need it.
Once it’s there, you can share that signal via a WiFi network, or by cable using a modem or router.


Before you start…

Food for thought: Sometimes we’re tempted to buy the cheapest option. Just remember that “buy cheap, buy twice” is especially true with tech. Make sure the antenna is actually right for your situation.


What do you need?

To know the lay of the land (geography).
To identify which carriers have the best signal.
A supplier for antennas.
A bit of cash.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Determine if you actually need an antenna

If you have a weak signal that gets better when you move a few meters, there might be cell towers nearby. Buying an antenna will help you get a stable connection.

Heads up: If there’s absolutely no mobile coverage at all, one of these antennas won’t magically create a signal.



Step 2 → Ask the key questions

Where am I located geographically?
First, understand the terrain. The antenna needs to have a “line of sight” with a tower. Find the nearest cell tower—they’re usually up on the ridges or hilltops.

Which carriers have coverage in the area?
Make sure to find the provider that actually works there. Ask your neighbors.
What space are you trying to get online?
We recommend focusing on public spaces like schools or libraries, since the internet benefits more people that way.


Step 3 → Identify the technical details

Know your topography
Get the exact coordinates of your location using a Smartphone. This info will be super useful when buying, so the supplier can give you better advice.
What should be in your kit?

A 3G/4G antenna (usually a Yagi type).
Mounting hardware.
Connection cable (like RG-6).
A Modem or Router.




Step 4 → Make the final call

Ask the seller about all the options. The most expensive one isn’t necessarily the one that will work best for you.

Don’t get fooled

Tip: Sellers sometimes push for more expensive solutions than you really need. Ask plenty of questions so you can make up your own mind.


How much is enough?
A single antenna and one connection, shared as a group, will be more than enough to enjoy everything the internet has to offer.

en/solve/solv-organize-space.title: How to set up a space for group internet access?
en/solve/solv-organize-space.summary: The look and feel of a space is key to getting us connected.
en/solve/solv-organize-space.content:
Hi! I’m Catalina, welcome 👋🏽
I wrote this solution because, over time, I’ve discovered how the objects around us shape the way we relate to one another. When I first got into SOLE, I didn’t just learn a methodology; I discovered a whole way of promoting group Internet use through small details (which aren’t actually that small), like how you set up a meeting space.
Have you ever heard of this idea of using the Internet as a group? At SOLE, we’re still figuring it out. For now, we know it has to do with people getting together to use the Internet, but also with the devices or spaces we use (or invent) to connect, share, and learn with the Internet, especially in person.
Shall we set up your next meeting space together? I’ll walk you through it! 👇🏽

What does it mean to set up a space for group Internet use?

⚠️ Before you start, it’s important to know which space you’re going to use. If you don’t have one yet, this solution can help you find one: How to get a community hall or any community space to use the internet as a group?

Setting up a space refers to how we organize the elements inside it: chairs, tables, whiteboards, posters, projectors, whatever.
To host a SOLE, for example, we need to dis-organize the space to keep it from looking like a classroom. This is important because, to promote different ways of learning, it’s crucial that people don’t feel like they’re in a traditional learning environment.
This matters because the way a space is organized generates different interactions between people. Think, for example, of a church versus a restaurant.
In a church, all the chairs are arranged in rows facing the front. It’s a space where attention is directed toward one person (the priest), and you’re not really supposed to chat with others; that’s why you’re shoulder to shoulder. In a restaurant, on the other hand, people are organized in small groups. There are chairs around various tables where everyone can see each other. It’s a space made for interacting, for chatting, and of course, for eating.

What is it for?
Planning how a space is organized encourages certain interactions over others. When it comes to using the Internet as a group, we want people to be able to share a computer or the network, but also ideas and experiences—in other words, conversations.
So yes, this solution helps you organize a space to allow for group Internet use. But it goes further! Using the Internet as a group allows for self-managed learning, planning, and carrying out community projects. If you browse the Internet as a group, it’s harder to fall for traps or fake content because there are more humans there to analyze the information. But you can also do things that seem simple, like watching a movie, which can have powerful results, like several people laughing at the same time.
In short, this solution promotes ways to (re)connect in a world where it’s becoming increasingly common to feel alone.

What do you need?

A space (your own or borrowed)
One table for every 4 people
More chairs than tables; enough for everyone (plastic ones are quite practical)
One computer for every 3-5 people (or at least tablets)
Webcam and microphone (one of the computers can work)
A whiteboard or space where you can write (it could also be glass, a window, a blank poster, etc.)
Markers


How to do it?
Rather than a specific step-by-step guide, I prefer to share some recommendations for setting up your space, as well as different ways to configure it and the interactions each one might trigger.

Recommendation #1 → Plan your meeting, get what you need.

Do you know how many people you’re expecting? Do you already have your activity planned?
Having a plan for what you’re going to do is key to knowing what you need.
Do you have tables, chairs, a whiteboard? If so, move on to the next step. If not, I can give you some tips on how to get them.
Community spaces usually have tables and chairs. Shops do too. You can ask to borrow them there, making it clear that you’ll take responsibility for them (you can leave a written note or document to put the owner at ease). If you choose to meet with people at a time when there aren’t many customers, it’s more likely they’ll lend them to you.
Another option is to use similar items. At SOLE, for example, we use fruit and vegetable crates to simulate tables and chairs. They’re great! And they can often be recycled.
— Photo of SOLE stools


Recommendation #2 → Dis-organize the space!

Using the Internet as a group should feel like something pleasant. Something people choose to do, not something they have to do. The best way to do this is by making the space feel flexible.
Take a look at these three different ways to configure the space:
— Photo of spaces
What do they remind you of? How do they make you feel? Here 👇🏽 I’ll share how I remember/feel them:

This is the usual layout of a classroom or conference room. There is one person (or several) at the front, usually addressing the audience in a “one-way” manner, meaning the audience is there mainly to listen, not to intervene. The interaction is more hierarchical: the person at the front has the attention.
The circle or semi-circle layout is, for example, how community meetings or dialogue circles are usually held. This way of positioning allows everyone to see each other and helps sound circulate and carry easily. This setup invites everyone to interact in a “multi-directional” way, making the bond between participants less hierarchical.
This is the usual layout of a SOLE or a restaurant. It’s a way of positioning that promotes several “small conversations” at the same time. Unlike the first two, this layout allows more people to speak, reducing the number of people involved in each specific interaction. This is an excellent option when we want to cover more topics in the same amount of time or, like in a SOLE, when several people want to focus their attention on something specific.

There are a thousand ways to configure a space. Even these three I’m sharing can be mixed together. What I want to show you is that different ways of organizing a space promote different interactions, but also different hierarchies between the people participating in the interaction.
At SOLE, rather than organizing, we like to “dis-organize” the space, because the ideal is that it never looks like a classroom or a community board meeting. In group Internet use, it’s key to promote horizontal (non-hierarchical) relationships, where you can chat within small groups, but also between groups.
— Photo of SOLE configuration.
I always recommend having a whiteboard or space to write that everyone can see. It works very well as a “memory aid” as conversations develop.

👆🏽 If you’re hosting a SOLE, you can use the materials from the SOLE Kit to give the space more personality. If it’s not a SOLE, I still recommend decorating with posters or materials that get people in tune with the energy of the activity.



Recommendation #3 → Invent and discover the best way to set up your spaces

In our experience, this last configuration is the one that has worked best for us to use the Internet as a group. But this is just one idea. Remember that if there’s one thing that defines a “cacharrero” (tinkerer), it’s the exercise of trial and error, so go ahead and try more combinations or new ways to configure your spaces! Surely there will be other ways that work even better for you. Just one condition: share them on Voltaje! (Just kidding, it’s not a requirement, but it would be very useful for other people 😋).
Good luck with your meeting!


How do you know if this solution works?
Think about what you had in mind when setting up your space. What was your goal? What did you expect to happen? Then (ideally at the end of the meeting), observe the space. What changed in it? What stayed the same?
There’s no magic formula to know if the space layout worked. But a good sign that it did is that the space has changed. Sometimes people (dis)organize the space even more. They move chairs, push tables together, find other places to write… Let them! That’s a great way to know that people are taking ownership of the place and that they felt the need to move through it as a result of the conversations they wanted to be part of.
Another way is during the meeting. It’s not always easy, but try to pay attention to the interactions between people: Where do they talk the most? Where do they laugh? Where do they reflect? Where do they rest? Pay attention to how the space is arranged every time you see different emotions unfolding.

Other possible Internets
Sometimes we dream not only of inventing new ways to configure the space, but also of new devices that allow us to interact even better with the Internet, but as a group. Can you imagine if there were a computer with four keyboards? What would we have to do to write a letter with four hands? What kind of video games could we play? How much more could we learn together?
—four-keyboard computer imagination.
Thinking up new physical ways to foster collective interactions is very powerful in a world where individual interactions are increasingly promoted. How do you design for communities and not just for individuals? What can we do as a group that we can’t do alone? What worlds can we invent and build together?
At SOLE, we’ve been “inventing” a physical space where the Internet can be used as a group. We call it the SOLE Lab. In fact, there are already three in Colombia!

⚡⚡ Learn about the experience of the most recent one in this inspiration: We built a SOLE Lab in La Guajira to use the Internet as a group, and the others in the “Get Inspired” section.

But we want more communities in Colombia and the world to have one! That’s why now, in 2026, we’re creating the “do-it-yourself” version of this space, which will be something like assembling furniture, but for a space.
—video SOLE Lab DIY
And what do you think? Hopefully, these questions encourage you to imagine other ways of relating to the Internet. Or as we say, other possible Internets!

Related solutions

Remember, if you don’t have a space yet, this solution might be useful: How to get a community hall or any community space to use the internet as a group? →
If you still don’t know how to invite people, check out this solution: How to write an invitation that gets people to show up? →
